D7-01.consequence: entity lane silent on possessive questions
D7-01.defect: Query tokenization keeps possessive `'s`: entity `Caroline's` never equals posting `Caroline`

D7-02.consequence: lowercase queries get no entity signal
D7-02.defect: Entity matching is case-sensitive (BINARY `=`) and query-side extraction requires a capital letter

D7-03.consequence: inflated BM25 noise and coverage floors
D7-03.defect: Folding `caroline's` yields a spurious term `s` with real df/tf

D7-04.defect: Support verdict demands ⌈50%⌉ literal term coverage on the delivered quote and discards ranked candidates

D7-05.consequence: governed evidence dies at the verdict
D7-05.defect: Pack-derived hits carry no signals (`score=0.0`, `unranked`) so the governed lane's own judgment is lost

D7-06.defect: Min–max normalization on a degenerate range maps every positive value to 1.0

D7-07.defect: Flat `entity_overlap` bonus rewards every document containing the speaker name

D7-08.defect: Typed-lane prefilter is a namespace-wide `LIKE '%term%'` scan beside an unused FTS5 index

D7-09.defect: Source lane (the only true BM25 + vector path) is skipped unless the typed lane is "thin"

D7-10.consequence: full-corpus statistics per query under write load
D7-10.defect: Projection fingerprint changes on every committed add, invalidating corpus-statistic memos

D7-11.defect: Each sub-lane truncates to 40 before fusion

D7-12.defect: Identifier support requires the literal surface form

D7-13.defect: Update-candidate detection runs a namespace scan inside the add write transaction

D7-14.defect: Three lane stages share one sequentially-derated deadline

D7-15.consequence: the most expensive queries are never cheap
D7-15.defect: `insufficient`/`partial` results are never cached; cache off by default

D7-16.defect: FTS5 uses `unicode61` only: no stemming, no trigram, no typo path

D7-17.defect: Dense lane skipped on the consumer path; hashing encoder is non-semantic; vectors scanned row-by-row in Python

D7-18.defect: Relative time phrases are detected and dropped with `ambiguous_time`, never resolved

D7-19.consequence: cannot weight or filter by speaker
D7-19.defect: No speaker/actor field in the lexical index; speaker text is ordinary content

D7-20.defect: Dialogue turns admitted through `require_review=True` never become active claims; claim lanes idle on consumer corpora

D7-21.defect: No session/conversation grouping of turns; no neighbor-turn context

D7-22.consequence: wasted I/O on the hot path
D7-22.defect: Payload bytes re-read and HMAC-verified twice per candidate (typed + materialization)

D7-23.defect: Two extra read snapshots + one write transaction per search (collapse, conflict labels, exposure)

D7-24.defect: No LoCoMo/LongMemEval/BEAM adapters; no reader/judge harness; no retrieval-metric suite for public data

B1.workload: 10,000 turns (≈ 17 LoCoMo conversations), S1 tier, feature rerank on

B1-cache.workload: B1 with the consumer result cache on, repeated intents

B1-neural.workload: B1 with S2 int8 transformer tier

B2.workload: B1 under load: 5 writes/s + 20 queries/s concurrent, managed drain

B4.workload: 1,000,000 units (~30–60M tokens), S1 int8, ANN permitted

V7-00.01.section_title: Authority and what V7 is allowed to change
V7-00.01.text: This file is approved for implementation only after owner sign-off. Approval of design does not authorize competitive claims, publication, provider activation, or paid usage.

V7-00.02.section_title: Authority and what V7 is allowed to change
V7-00.02.text: V7 MAY change default ranking, default lanes, default indexes, tokenization, the support verdict, pack formats, and recommended profiles for `local_memory` and the new profiles `local_memory_quality` and `local_memory_max` (V7-21.04). It MUST NOT weaken quote permission, purpose constraints, eligibility-before-rank, authorization-local statistics (V4-28.03 / F4-11 / V5-11 / V6-02.04), quarantine cascade, consent-gated hydration, or deletion closure.

V7-00.03.section_title: Authority and what V7 is allowed to change
V7-00.03.text: Requirements use `V7-NN.MM`; scenarios `H01`–`H104`; gates `G7-00`–`G7-14`; envelopes `B0`–`B6`; defects `D7-01`–`D7-40`. These namespaces MUST NOT overwrite V2–V6 identifiers or evidence.

V7-00.04.section_title: Authority and what V7 is allowed to change
V7-00.04.text: The following actions each require a recorded owner authorization before execution: (a) downloading any model weights; (b) downloading or storing any dataset whose license is not OSI-permissive or CC-BY (LoCoMo is CC BY-NC 4.0 — V7-22.03); (c) any paid API call (reader, judge, extractor, embedder, reranker, hosted comparator); (d) any network egress from a store-holding process; (e) publication of any benchmark number or comparative sentence. The authorization record names the action, scope, budget, and expiry, and is stored under `eval/v7/authorizations/`.

V7-00.05.section_title: Authority and what V7 is allowed to change
V7-00.05.text: Importing `verbatim` MUST still create no files, threads, sockets, or downloads (V6-00.04). Constructing `Memory` remains the explicit activation seam. Model loading is lazy and never on import.

V7-00.06.section_title: Authority and what V7 is allowed to change
V7-00.06.text: Every V7 requirement MUST land in the V7 ledger (`eval/v7/`) with `owner`, `code_surfaces`, `scenarios`, `evidence_type`, and an honest `qualification_status` from the V6 vocabulary plus `deferred` (owner + reason mandatory, V6 F31 rule). `qualified` requires named executed evidence from the declared gate procedure.

V7-00.07.section_title: Authority and what V7 is allowed to change
V7-00.07.text: Measurements MUST run on a quiet tree (V6-00.07). Additionally, every quality number MUST be produced from a frozen run manifest (V7-22.10) whose digest is printed next to the number wherever it appears, including internal notes.

V7-00.08.section_title: Authority and what V7 is allowed to change
V7-00.08.text: Where V7 changes a contract a predecessor stated differently, the V7 text governs and MUST name the superseded requirement id. This file supersedes: V6-02.01 (typed-index-first as the *only* first stage — V7-05.03 makes all enabled lanes peers), V6-03.01 (install default encoder — V7-07.02 adds a distilled static tier), V6-02.14's 25 ms A0 target (restated as envelopes B0/B1 in §17.1, with the same no-silent-change rule).

V7-00.09.section_title: Authority and what V7 is allowed to change
V7-00.09.text: A V7 release MAY ship while some gates miss, but MUST say which. It MUST NOT relabel a missed quality gate as a latency win or vice versa; each axis is reported on its own row.

V7-00.10.section_title: Authority and what V7 is allowed to change
V7-00.10.text: Competitor facts in §01 are dated snapshots. Before any external use, each quoted figure MUST be re-fetched from its primary source and the fetch date updated; a figure older than 90 days is `stale` and cannot back a claim (V4-59.07 TTL carried).

V7-00.11.section_title: Authority and what V7 is allowed to change
V7-00.11.text: The model-free default is a hypothesis. `local_memory` MAY ship without any model. `local_memory_quality` MUST NOT claim SB-04, SB-05, or SB-09 on T0 alone unless the fact-index ablation (V7-13.19) shows that quote-verified extracted lines do not beat T0 units by more than 0.01 any@10; if they do, the quality profile's claim requires the extracted-line unit (T2 or an equivalent producer) and says so.

V7-01.01.section_title: The market as measured — competitor fact register (2026-09-22 snapshot)
V7-01.01.text: **The reader dominates headline accuracy.** Hindsight moves 83.6 → 91.4 on LongMemEval by changing only the backbone; Mastra moves 84.23 → 94.87 the same way; full-context OSS-20B scores 39.0. Every V7 quality number MUST therefore be reported per reader model, with the reader held identical across compared arms (V7-22.14). A comparison with different readers is `invalid`, never a win.

V7-01.02.section_title: The market as measured — competitor fact register (2026-09-22 snapshot)
V7-01.02.text: **Prompts can buy 20 points.** The independent Mem0 reproduction (73.8 vs 93.4) traced the gap to dataset-specific answer rules, hidden chain-of-thought, and a lenient judge. V7 MUST ship a neutral reference reader and judge (V7-15.07, V7-22.16) and MUST NOT contain any rule, example, synonym list, or equivalence keyed to benchmark question ids, gold answers, or benchmark-specific phrasings (V7-22.18 tripwire).

V7-01.03.section_title: The market as measured — competitor fact register (2026-09-22 snapshot)
V7-01.03.text: **Retrieval is necessary but not sufficient.** Every 90%+ system combines write-time structure (dated facts, events, observations), multi-signal retrieval, reranking, and a capable reader. V7 attacks all four and reports each separately (V7-22.12).

V7-01.04.section_title: The market as measured — competitor fact register (2026-09-22 snapshot)
V7-01.04.text: **Time is the swing category.** Mem0's largest claimed gains are temporal — the cited deltas (+29.3 LoCoMo, +45.9 LME) are the vendor's new-vs-old algorithm totals (platform, incl. the temporal stack); the vendor-documented temporal-classifier component alone is +4.1 overall / +6.7 temporal / −1.9 open-domain, platform-only (V75-07.04). Chronos's event calendar is worth +58.9% on its baseline; the LongMemEval paper's time-aware query expansion is its highest-ROI technique. V7-09 makes temporal resolution deterministic, dual-axis, and first-class.

V7-01.05.section_title: The market as measured — competitor fact register (2026-09-22 snapshot)
V7-01.05.text: **Every leader pays an LLM on every write.** Hindsight retain is 0.5–2 s per batch with minutes-long consolidation backlogs in the field; Mem0 extraction is an LLM call per add; Zep calls several per episode. V7's default write path is model-free and its optional model path is asynchronous, bounded, and grounded (V7-13).

V7-01.06.section_title: The market as measured — competitor fact register (2026-09-22 snapshot)
V7-01.06.text: **Their recall costs 0.1–1 s.** Hindsight 100–600 ms, Zep p95 632 ms, Mem0 p50 880 ms. V7 targets p95 ≤ 60 ms at 100K memories without a cross-encoder and ≤ 150 ms with one (V7-17), on a 4-core CPU.

V7-01.07.section_title: The market as measured — competitor fact register (2026-09-22 snapshot)
V7-01.07.text: **Nobody grounds to bytes.** Hindsight's observations carry quotes and a proof count, but facts are LLM paraphrases; Mem0 records have no source pointer; Graphiti facts point to episodes, not spans. V7 keeps span pins mandatory for every delivered fact (V6-02.02 carried; V7-13.06).

V7-01.08.section_title: The market as measured — competitor fact register (2026-09-22 snapshot)
V7-01.08.text: **Security is an enterprise upsell elsewhere.** Hindsight's prompt-injection blocking is Cloud-Enterprise-only; its OSS defense is 45 regexes, off by default, not retroactive. V7 ships measured write-channel and retrieval-time poisoning defense on by default in OSS (V7-19).

V7-01.09.section_title: The market as measured — competitor fact register (2026-09-22 snapshot)
V7-01.09.text: **Benchmarks are moving to actions and cost.** DolphinBench scores task completion with total cost and median latency on the same leaderboard; LongMemEval-V2 scores an accuracy–latency frontier. V7 MUST report cost and latency beside every accuracy (V7-22.20) and MUST run DolphinBench through the Hermes harness it already integrates with (V7-22.06).

V7-01.10.section_title: The market as measured — competitor fact register (2026-09-22 snapshot)
V7-01.10.text: **Category labels are a trap.** LoCoMo's integer categories do not follow the paper's order (source code: 1 = multi-hop, 2 = temporal, 3 = open-domain, 4 = single-hop, 5 = adversarial; snap-research/locomo issue #29); vendors publish open-domain scores ranging from 70.83 to 95.12 that are not obviously the same slice. V7 reports LoCoMo by integer id AND name, with the mapping printed in every table (V7-22.07).

V7-03.01.section_title: The winning thesis and the scoreboard
V7-03.01.text: The scoreboard is the V7 north star. Each SB row MUST map to a gate (§26), an eval suite (§22), and a published row in `eval/v7/report_v7.md` that shows pass/miss, the measured value, the reference, the protocol, and the manifest digest. A missing row is `not_run`, never omitted.

V7-03.02.section_title: The winning thesis and the scoreboard
V7-03.02.text: Track Q rows that require a paid or downloaded reader stay `blocked_on_authorization` until V7-00.04 is satisfied; Track R, B-envelope, trust, and determinism rows MUST be executable without any network access or model (owned twins always; public datasets once O1/O2 are decided and the files are local).

V7-03.03.section_title: The winning thesis and the scoreboard
V7-03.03.text: A row may be claimed only on the full claimed split (V5-21.06 carried). LongMemEval-S means all 500 questions; LoCoMo cat 1–4 means all 1,540; subsets are labeled with their size and cannot back an SB claim.

V7-03.04.section_title: The winning thesis and the scoreboard
V7-03.04.text: Every SB row reports quality **and** tokens **and** latency **and** cost on the same line (V7-01.09). A quality win bought with more tokens than the reference must say so.

V7-04.01.section_title: Architecture — what the V7 hot path looks like
V7-04.01.text: The read path above is normative in shape: stage names, order, and per-stage budgets MUST appear in the stage profiler (`eval/v7/stage_profile.py`) and every B-envelope artifact. A stage that exceeds its p95 slice on B1 for two consecutive measured runs is a named defect.

V7-04.02.section_title: Architecture — what the V7 hot path looks like
V7-04.02.text: No stage may issue a network call on the default profiles. Optional model stages (S5, neural L-dense, T1/T2) run only in profiles that declare them and only with provisioned, hash-verified artifacts (V7-07.10).

V7-04.03.section_title: Architecture — what the V7 hot path looks like
V7-04.03.text: Every stage MUST honor the request `Deadline`, report `ok | skipped(reason) | partial(examined, eligible) | unavailable(reason) | deadline`, and never widen authorization when it degrades. A degraded stage lowers `coverage` honestly; it MUST NOT turn a result `ready`.

V7-04.04.section_title: Architecture — what the V7 hot path looks like
V7-04.04.text: The read path is one function family in one module tree (`verbatim/retrieval/v7/`), reached by `Memory.search`, the service, MCP, and every adapter. No surface may assemble its own ranking.

V7-05.01.section_title: Retrieval core — lanes as peers, never as fallbacks
V7-05.01.text: The consumer `search` MUST run every lane enabled by the active profile on every query (subject only to deadline and declared policy). V6-02.01's "typed index first, source lane as fallback" is superseded.

V7-05.02.section_title: Retrieval core — lanes as peers, never as fallbacks
V7-05.02.text: Lane enablement MUST be a declared, versioned policy table (`retrieval_policy/v7`) keyed by profile and query intent class, not code-path conditionals. The table is printed in `coverage.policy` on every result.

V7-05.03.section_title: Retrieval core — lanes as peers, never as fallbacks
V7-05.03.text: The `thin` / `run_source` gate (`memory/facade.py:1783-1819`, D7-09) MUST be removed. A test proves that, on a corpus where the typed lane returns a full pool, the lexical and dense lanes still contribute candidates and appear in `coverage.lanes` as `ok`.

V7-05.04.section_title: Retrieval core — lanes as peers, never as fallbacks
V7-05.04.text: Lanes MUST produce ranked candidate lists with per-candidate raw signals; fusion (V7-10) consumes ranks and signals, never lane-local normalized scores.

V7-05.05.section_title: Retrieval core — lanes as peers, never as fallbacks
V7-05.05.text: Deadline allocation MUST be per-lane slices computed at S2 entry from the remaining budget and the policy table (e.g., proportional to declared lane cost), not the sequential re-derating of D7-14. A slow lane consumes only its own slice.

V7-05.06.section_title: Retrieval core — lanes as peers, never as fallbacks
V7-05.06.text: Lanes that are independent SHOULD share a single read snapshot and one statement cache; a lane MUST NOT open its own transaction on the hot path.

V7-05.07.section_title: Retrieval core — lanes as peers, never as fallbacks
V7-05.07.text: Candidate pool size per lane is governed by `budget` (V7-21.06): low = 50, mid = 200, high = 800 candidates per lane before fusion (D7-11 superseded). The cap is a policy value, printed in coverage.

V7-05.08.section_title: Retrieval core — lanes as peers, never as fallbacks
V7-05.08.text: Eligibility (authorization, purpose, holds, quarantine cascade, suppression, lifecycle, generation) MUST be evaluated before rank on every lane (V4 carried). Approximate candidate generation is allowed; approximate eligibility is a security defect.

V7-05.09.section_title: Retrieval core — lanes as peers, never as fallbacks
V7-05.09.text: Every lane MUST have an ablation switch honored by the eval harness (`lanes_disabled=[...]`), and the V7 retrieval suite MUST publish a leave-one-lane-out table on LoCoMo and LongMemEval-S (Track R).

V7-05.10.section_title: Retrieval core — lanes as peers, never as fallbacks
V7-05.10.text: Query and document normalization MUST share one analyzer (`norm/v2`) that: casefolds; applies NFKC; splits English possessives and clitics (`'s`, `’s`, `n't`, `'re`, `'ll`, `'ve`, `'d`) into base token + dropped clitic; never emits single-letter clitic tokens as terms (D7-01, D7-03); preserves exact identifiers (URLs, hashes, versions, code spans) on a separate channel untouched by folding. `norm/v1` rows remain readable; mixed-version stores re-project under the generation fence.

V7-05.11.section_title: Retrieval core — lanes as peers, never as fallbacks
V7-05.11.text: The analyzer MUST expose deterministic, versioned stopword handling: stopwords are indexed (so phrase queries work) but carry an IDF-derived weight; no hard-coded "drop" list may remove a term that has df below the corpus median.

V7-05.12.section_title: Retrieval core — lanes as peers, never as fallbacks
V7-05.12.text: Query intent classification (`intent/v2`) MUST classify at least: `lookup`, `identifier`, `temporal_point`, `temporal_range`, `temporal_order`, `duration`, `count_aggregate`, `current_value`, `history_of`, `preference`, `comparison`, `multi_hop`, `open_domain`, `why/causal`, `abstain_likely`. Classes select lane weights and pack shape; they never gate eligibility. The classifier is deterministic (rules + lexicons) and ships with a labeled fixture of ≥ 600 queries at ≥ 0.90 macro-accuracy.

V7-05.13.section_title: Retrieval core — lanes as peers, never as fallbacks
V7-05.13.text: Multi-hop and comparison intents MUST trigger deterministic decomposition: entity- and conjunction-based facet sub-queries (≤ 3), each run through S2–S4, merged by RRF with facet coverage bonus; each facet is disclosed in `coverage.facets`.

V7-05.14.section_title: Retrieval core — lanes as peers, never as fallbacks
V7-05.14.text: A second retrieval round (pseudo-relevance feedback, RM3-style: top-5, ≤ 10 expansion terms, weight ≤ 0.5) MAY run when the top-3 fused margin is below a calibrated threshold or the class is `open_domain`; it MUST be ablated and ship on only if the paired Track R gain is ≥ +0.02 any@10 with no category regressing > 0.01.

V7-05.15.section_title: Retrieval core — lanes as peers, never as fallbacks
V7-05.15.text: The whole S1–S8 pipeline MUST be callable in `explain=True` mode returning, per delivered item: lane ranks, raw signals, fused score, rerank score, boosts, verdict reason, and pack decision — the Hindsight `trace` equivalent, but byte-stable.

V7-06.01.section_title: Lexical engine — real BM25F, stems, trigrams, typo tolerance
V7-06.01.text: The source FTS index MUST add a Porter-stemmed shadow column (or a second FTS5 table with `tokenize='porter unicode61 remove_diacritics 2'`) and query both exact and stemmed forms; exact matches receive a declared bonus over stem-only matches.

V7-06.02.section_title: Lexical engine — real BM25F, stems, trigrams, typo tolerance
V7-06.02.text: The lexical index MUST be fielded: at minimum `text`, `speaker` (actor/role/display name), `entities` (canonical keys + aliases), `session` (session label/title), and `when` (normalized date tokens: `2023-05-07`, `2023-05`, `2023`, `may`, `sunday`). BM25F column weights are a versioned policy (`bm25f/v1`, defaults text 1.0, entities 0.8, speaker 0.3, when 0.6, session 0.2) tuned only on the dev split (V7-22.09).

V7-06.03.section_title: Lexical engine — real BM25F, stems, trigrams, typo tolerance
V7-06.03.text: The typed-lane token prefilter (D7-08) MUST use the FTS5 index (`MATCH`) instead of `LIKE '%term%'`; the typed lane's candidate set is the intersection of FTS postings with typed-record keys.

V7-06.04.section_title: Lexical engine — real BM25F, stems, trigrams, typo tolerance
V7-06.04.text: A trigram FTS5 shadow (`tokenize='trigram'`) MUST exist for the text column. For any query term with df = 0 (or df below a calibrated floor), the fuzzy lane MUST retrieve respellings with edit distance ≤ 2 (≤ 1 for terms of ≤ 5 characters) from the `fts5vocab` term table and reissue them as low-weight alternatives. "persue" → "pursue" is fixture H07.

V7-06.05.section_title: Lexical engine — real BM25F, stems, trigrams, typo tolerance
V7-06.05.text: BM25 parameters default to k1 = 1.2, b = 0.75 (per field b in `bm25f/v1`), with N, df, and avgdl computed over the request-eligible corpus (V6-02.04 carried). Per-scope FTS5 tables are permitted only when the index universe is provably the eligible set.

V7-06.06.section_title: Lexical engine — real BM25F, stems, trigrams, typo tolerance
V7-06.06.text: Corpus statistics MUST be maintained incrementally (df and length sums updated in the same generation-fenced transaction as the posting write), keyed by scope and generation, so a committed add updates statistics in O(terms of the add) and never forces full-corpus recomputation at query time (D7-10). Statistics memos are keyed by `(scope, generation, stats_version)`, not by a corpus fingerprint that every add invalidates.

V7-06.07.section_title: Lexical engine — real BM25F, stems, trigrams, typo tolerance
V7-06.07.text: When the eligible set differs from the index universe (holds, purpose filters, suppression), the lane MUST correct statistics by subtracting ineligible contributions from maintained aggregates (bounded by the ineligible count), or fall back to exact computation with `coverage.lexical.stats = exact_recomputed`. It MUST NOT silently use universe statistics (V6-02.04).

V7-06.08.section_title: Lexical engine — real BM25F, stems, trigrams, typo tolerance
V7-06.08.text: Phrase and proximity: quoted query spans and adjacent-term pairs MUST score a phrase bonus via FTS5 `NEAR`/phrase queries; the bonus is a feature-rerank signal (V7-10.07), not a lane.

V7-06.09.section_title: Lexical engine — real BM25F, stems, trigrams, typo tolerance
V7-06.09.text: The lexical lane MUST return up to the budget cap with scores that are raw BM25F values (not normalized) plus matched-term lists for explanation.

V7-06.10.section_title: Lexical engine — real BM25F, stems, trigrams, typo tolerance
V7-06.10.text: Performance: L-lex p95 ≤ 6 ms at 10K and ≤ 12 ms at 100K memories on the reference machine for queries of ≤ 12 terms, measured in the B-envelopes.

V7-06.11.section_title: Lexical engine — real BM25F, stems, trigrams, typo tolerance
V7-06.11.text: Every new index (stem, trigram, fielded rows, statistics tables) MUST participate in deletion closure, secure-delete, quarantine, and generation fencing; a purge MUST remove the erased text from `fts5vocab`-visible terms when no other eligible row uses them (closure verify checks vocab).

V7-07.01.section_title: Dense engine — semantic recall without a network
V7-07.01.text: The dense lane MUST run on every `search` in profiles `local_memory_quality` and `local_memory_max`, and in `local_memory` whenever a semantic tier ≥ S1 is provisioned (V7-07.02). Coverage reports the tier.

V7-07.02.section_title: Dense engine — semantic recall without a network
V7-07.02.text: Encoder tiers, each with its own `encoder_id`, calibration entry, and envelope:

V7-07.03.section_title: Dense engine — semantic recall without a network
V7-07.03.text: A tier is `recommended` for a profile only after a paired Track R run shows strictly higher any@10 than the tier below on LoCoMo **and** LongMemEval-S with no category regression > 0.01 (V6-03.10 pattern carried). Otherwise it stays available-but-unrecommended with the loss published.

V7-07.04.section_title: Dense engine — semantic recall without a network
V7-07.04.text: Document vectors MUST be stored as a contiguous per-`(encoder_id, scope, generation)` matrix (packed float32 or int8 blocks, row index → `(source_id, revision)`), memory-mappable or loaded once per snapshot, with per-row BLOBs kept only as the durable oracle. Per-row BLOB decoding on the hot path is prohibited above 2,000 eligible rows (D7-17).

V7-07.05.section_title: Dense engine — semantic recall without a network
V7-07.05.text: Scoring MUST be batched: with numpy present, one matrix–vector product per block; without numpy, an `array('f')`-based blocked loop whose output ordering is proven identical to the oracle on a fixed corpus. Ties break on `(-score, source_id, revision)`.

V7-07.06.section_title: Dense engine — semantic recall without a network
V7-07.06.text: Quantization: int8 scalar (per-dimension or per-row scale) scan + float32 rescore of the top 4×K is the default at > 20K rows; binary (sign) codes + popcount + float32 rescore of the top 8×K is permitted at > 200K rows. Each mode publishes measured recall@K loss versus the exact oracle on the eval corpus; loss > 1.0 percentage point at K = 50 fails its gate.

V7-07.07.section_title: Dense engine — semantic recall without a network
V7-07.07.text: ANN (HNSW via `usearch`/`hnswlib`, or `sqlite-vec` rescore index) MAY be enabled only above 200K eligible rows or after a measured exact-scan miss of the L-dense budget (V6-02.05 carried), only on a provably eligible partition or with post-filter plus exact rescore, and only as an accelerator: eligibility, quarantine, and HMAC checks stay exact. ANN recall@50 vs exact ≥ 0.97 is required.

V7-07.08.section_title: Dense engine — semantic recall without a network
V7-07.08.text: Matryoshka truncation MAY be used for the first-stage scan (e.g., 256 of 1,024 dims) with full-dimension rescore; the truncation dimension is part of `encoder_id`.

V7-07.09.section_title: Dense engine — semantic recall without a network
V7-07.09.text: Contextual embedding text: every embedded unit MUST be prefixed with a deterministic context header (`<date> | <speaker> | <session label>: `) before encoding (the zero-model form of contextual retrieval); the header format is versioned in `encoder_id`.

V7-07.10.section_title: Dense engine — semantic recall without a network
V7-07.10.text: Model artifacts are provisioned only by an explicit `verbatim models fetch <id>` (owner-authorized, V7-00.04) or a local path; every file is sha256-pinned in a manifest with license id; `latest` revisions, remote code, pickle, and `trust_remote_code` are rejected; `available()` is true only after verification. Import and `Memory()` never download.

V7-07.11.section_title: Dense engine — semantic recall without a network
V7-07.11.text: Licenses: only Apache-2.0, MIT, BSD, or CC-BY model weights may be marked `recommended`. Non-commercial (e.g., CC-BY-NC) or custom-terms weights (e.g., Gemma terms) require an explicit owner legal flag and are never defaults.

V7-07.12.section_title: Dense engine — semantic recall without a network
V7-07.12.text: Embedding generation stays asynchronous (`source_embed` job); add-ack never includes model inference. Lexical visibility never waits for embeddings; a search before embeddings land reports `coverage.dense = partial(n_pending)` without blocking.

V7-07.13.section_title: Dense engine — semantic recall without a network
V7-07.13.text: Determinism: S0/S1 vectors are bit-exact across platforms; S2/S3 vectors are compared with a per-backend epsilon in golden tests; stored vectors from a different runtime/quantization are `excluded_generation`, never mixed into one space.

V7-07.14.section_title: Dense engine — semantic recall without a network
V7-07.14.text: RSS budget: resident vector structures ≤ rows × dims × bytes_per_dim × 1.2 + 32 MB; at 100K × 384 int8 this is ≤ 78 MB. Retain-time embedding buffers MUST be `array('f')`/numpy, never Python `list[float]` (the Hindsight #3756 failure mode, 7.7× overhead).

V7-07.15.section_title: Dense engine — semantic recall without a network
V7-07.15.text: Optional caller-supplied query vectors or hypothetical-answer text (HyDE-style) MAY be accepted as an additional dense query (`search(..., hint=...)`); Verbatim never generates them internally on default profiles.

V7-08.01.section_title: Entity and graph engine — resolution without a model, traversal without a graph database
V7-08.01.text: Every entity posting MUST carry a canonical key: `canon = fold(NFKC(casefold(strip_possessive(surface))))` plus the exact surface form. Matching on the hot path uses `canon`; exact-surface matches earn a declared bonus. D7-02 is closed when a lowercase, possessive, or re-cased query mention reaches the same postings as the original.

V7-08.02.section_title: Entity and graph engine — resolution without a model, traversal without a graph database
V7-08.02.text: Query-side entity extraction MUST NOT require capitalization. It MUST recognize any query token or n-gram (≤ 4 tokens) whose `canon` exists in the scope's entity vocabulary, in addition to capitalized-run detection.

V7-08.03.section_title: Entity and graph engine — resolution without a model, traversal without a graph database
V7-08.03.text: An alias table (`entity_aliases_v7(scope_id, canon, alias_canon, rule_id, evidence_count, method, state, generation)` — §30; the V1 `entity_aliases` name is taken) MUST be built by deterministic rules: (a) token-subset of a longer name within the same scope (`alice` ⊂ `alice chen`) when unambiguous; (b) initial forms (`alice c.`); (c) edit-distance ≤ 1 for names ≥ 6 characters with ≥ 2 shared co-occurring entities; (d) explicit user/agent statements ("call me Mel", "Melanie (Mel)") captured by patterns; (e) caller-supplied aliases. Ambiguous merges (two candidate canonicals) are never auto-applied; they become reviewable `alias_candidates`.

V7-08.04.section_title: Entity and graph engine — resolution without a model, traversal without a graph database
V7-08.04.text: Aliases expand queries at S1 (bounded to 8 expansions per mention) and are reported in `coverage.entities`. Merges are links, never rewrites of stored text; unmerging is a first-class operation.

V7-08.05.section_title: Entity and graph engine — resolution without a model, traversal without a graph database
V7-08.05.text: Speaker identity: the `speaker` field of each turn MUST be resolved to an entity canon; `speaker:<canon>` postings let queries like "What did Caroline say about…" filter or boost by speaker rather than by text mention.

V7-08.06.section_title: Entity and graph engine — resolution without a model, traversal without a graph database
V7-08.06.text: Entity signals MUST be IDF-weighted at the scope level: a canon present in > 30% of eligible units contributes at most 0.1 of the weight of a rare canon (closing D7-07). The speaker-name dominance fixture (H12) proves a question naming a frequent speaker ranks the evidence turn above ≥ 90% of non-evidence turns that merely mention the speaker.

V7-08.07.section_title: Entity and graph engine — resolution without a model, traversal without a graph database
V7-08.07.text: Graph edges MUST be maintained as typed, weighted, generation-fenced rows: `co_mention` (units sharing a canon, weight by inverse canon frequency), `same_session`, `adjacent_turn` (t±1, t±2), `temporal_near` (occurred intervals within a declared window), `semantic_knn` (top-k dense neighbors per unit computed by a background job, k ≤ 8, similarity ≥ calibrated floor), `supersedes`/`contradicts`/`refines` (V5 update relations), and `causal` (only from explicit causal connectives — "because", "so", "due to", "which is why" — with both clauses pinned; never inferred by a model on default profiles).

V7-08.08.section_title: Entity and graph engine — resolution without a model, traversal without a graph database
V7-08.08.text: The graph lane MUST implement bounded personalized PageRank (≤ 2–3 power iterations, damping 0.5, seeds = S2 top entity/lexical hits, frontier ≤ 400 nodes, edges restricted to eligible units) with per-edge-type weights in a versioned policy; it returns ranked units with the contributing path summarized for `explain`.

V7-08.09.section_title: Entity and graph engine — resolution without a model, traversal without a graph database
V7-08.09.text: The graph lane's link-expansion score for a unit MUST be decomposable into entity overlap, kNN weight, temporal proximity, and causal weight (Hindsight's decomposition, deterministic here) so each component is ablatable.

V7-08.10.section_title: Entity and graph engine — resolution without a model, traversal without a graph database
V7-08.10.text: Performance: L-graph p95 ≤ 6 ms at 10K and ≤ 15 ms at 100K units; edges stored with covering indexes `(scope, src, type)`; `semantic_knn` rebuild is incremental per added unit.

V7-08.11.section_title: Entity and graph engine — resolution without a model, traversal without a graph database
V7-08.11.text: Graph rows are derived artifacts: purge of a unit removes its incident edges in the same closure; quarantine of a unit removes it from traversal; tests prove no path through a held or purged unit can surface its neighbors' content via that unit.

V7-08.12.section_title: Entity and graph engine — resolution without a model, traversal without a graph database
V7-08.12.text: Multi-hop fixture: on LoCoMo cat 1 (multi-hop) Track R, the graph lane MUST contribute ≥ +0.08 any@10 over the graph-off arm, or it ships off by default with the ablation published.

V7-08.13.section_title: Entity and graph engine — resolution without a model, traversal without a graph database
V7-08.13.text: **Entity-resolution formula search arm.** Beside the `alias/v1` rules, the formula search (§32.0) MUST evaluate a weighted resolution score of the Hindsight form (`w_n·name_similarity + w_c·co-occurrence_overlap + w_r·recency`, threshold τ, abstain-to-new-entity below τ) and at least one variant with our canonical folding, on an owned fixture that includes same-name-different-person pairs (≥ 100), nickname/initial variants (≥ 100), and pronoun-only mentions. The selected method MUST abstain (leave two canonicals separate, or file an `alias_candidate`) whenever two canonicals remain plausible; its over-merge rate on the same-name fixture is published and MUST be ≤ 0.01.

V7-08.14.section_title: Entity and graph engine — resolution without a model, traversal without a graph database
V7-08.14.text: **Causal candidates.** Explicit-connective causal edges (V7-08.07) are the T0 floor. Model-proposed causal links (T1/T2) MAY be stored only as `causal_candidate` rows carrying quote pins for both clauses; they are never eligibility inputs, never delivered as statements, and enter the graph lane only after an ablation shows a Track R gain on `why/causal` questions with no other category regressing by more than 0.01. Until then the parity-matrix cell for causal links reads `floor only`.

V7-09.01.section_title: Temporal engine — two clocks, resolved at write, resolved at query, reasoned deterministically
V7-09.01.text: Every unit MUST carry two time axes: **recorded** (when Verbatim learned it: `recorded_at`, from the add timestamp or the message's own timestamp) and **occurred** (when the described event happened: an interval `[occurred_start, occurred_end]` with a precision grade `instant | day | week | month | season | year | decade | unknown` and a source `explicit | resolved_relative | session_default | unknown`).

V7-09.02.section_title: Temporal engine — two clocks, resolved at write, resolved at query, reasoned deterministically
V7-09.02.text: `add` MUST accept `occurred_at`, `session_id`, `session_started_at`, `message_at`, and `speaker` (typed arguments, not only metadata) so conversational imports preserve structure; adapters (Mem0 shim, Hermes, LangChain, importers) map their native fields onto them.

V7-09.03.section_title: Temporal engine — two clocks, resolved at write, resolved at query, reasoned deterministically
V7-09.03.text: `temporal/v2` MUST resolve, against the unit's anchor (`message_at` ∨ `session_started_at` ∨ `recorded_at`): absolute dates in common formats; weekday names ("on Sunday"); `yesterday/today/tomorrow/tonight`; `last/next/this` + {week, month, year, weekend, season, weekday}; `N {days|weeks|months|years} ago/later`; `in N …`; month names with or without year (nearest past occurrence, ties past-ward — V5 rule carried); seasons (meteorological by hemisphere setting, default northern); `a few days ago` (interval 2–5 days, precision week); ordinal expressions ("the first week of June"); ranges ("from May to July"). Every resolution records the anchor and rule id; unresolvable phrases are kept with `precision=unknown`, never dropped.

V7-09.04.section_title: Temporal engine — two clocks, resolved at write, resolved at query, reasoned deterministically
V7-09.04.text: Resolution MUST be deterministic and locale-pinned (English/Gregorian in v2; other locales declared unavailable) and covered by a fixture of ≥ 800 expressions with gold intervals, ≥ 0.97 exact-interval accuracy.

V7-09.05.section_title: Temporal engine — two clocks, resolved at write, resolved at query, reasoned deterministically
V7-09.05.text: At query time the same resolver MUST turn the question's time expressions into a query window anchored at `query_time` (caller-supplied `as_of`/`now`, or the benchmark's question date, or wall clock), closing D7-18. The resolved window, anchor, and rule appear in `coverage.temporal`.

V7-09.06.section_title: Temporal engine — two clocks, resolved at write, resolved at query, reasoned deterministically
V7-09.06.text: The temporal lane MUST retrieve units whose occurred interval overlaps the window (and, secondarily, whose recorded time does), select by lexical/dense relevance within the window (not by recency), and spread selection across the window with time buckets (≥ 4 buckets for windows > 1 month) so a "what happened in 2023" query is representative — Hindsight's rule, adopted.

V7-09.07.section_title: Temporal engine — two clocks, resolved at write, resolved at query, reasoned deterministically
V7-09.07.text: A temporal proximity signal (distance from the window centre relative to half-width) and a recency signal (bounded, V7-10.10) are feature-rerank inputs; recency MUST NOT be applied to queries with an explicit past window.

V7-09.08.section_title: Temporal engine — two clocks, resolved at write, resolved at query, reasoned deterministically
V7-09.08.text: **Event records** (the deterministic Chronos event calendar): for each unit, `event/v1` extracts zero or more `(subject_canon, predicate_lemma, object_text, polarity, occurred interval, pins)` tuples using rules over the normalized text (first-person and third-person patterns, speaker substitution for "I/me/my", common life-event lexicons: moved, started, joined, quit, married, bought, visited, adopted, graduated, painted, ran, signed up, …). Every tuple element is span-pinned; tuples failing pin verification are dropped. Event records are indexed by subject, predicate, and interval.

V7-09.09.section_title: Temporal engine — two clocks, resolved at write, resolved at query, reasoned deterministically
V7-09.09.text: Temporal intents MUST use the event index first: `temporal_point` ("when did X …") ranks events whose subject/predicate match and returns their interval; `temporal_order` ("which came first") returns the two events and their order; `duration` ("how long between") returns both intervals and the computed difference; `count_aggregate` over time ("how many times did …") returns the distinct matching events.

V7-09.10.section_title: Temporal engine — two clocks, resolved at write, resolved at query, reasoned deterministically
V7-09.10.text: A deterministic interval-algebra module (`temporal/algebra`) MUST implement containment, overlap, before/after, meets, duration (days/weeks/months/years with calendar-correct arithmetic), age-at-date, and relative phrasing ("two weeks before May 7, 2023"), with ≥ 400 unit tests and a property test suite. Computed results appear in packs as `computed` items with the formula and the pinned inputs (V7-12.09).

V7-09.11.section_title: Temporal engine — two clocks, resolved at write, resolved at query, reasoned deterministically
V7-09.11.text: Current vs historical: for `current_value` intents, units whose facts are superseded (V5 supersession, V7-16 state keys) are demoted and labeled `historical`; for `history_of` intents both are delivered in chronological order.

V7-09.12.section_title: Temporal engine — two clocks, resolved at write, resolved at query, reasoned deterministically
V7-09.12.text: Temporal precision is carried into answers: a month-precision event MUST NOT be rendered as a specific day by any Verbatim computed answer; the reference reader prompt instructs the same (V7-15.07).

V7-09.13.section_title: Temporal engine — two clocks, resolved at write, resolved at query, reasoned deterministically
V7-09.13.text: Track R temporal target: LoCoMo cat 2 any@10 ≥ 0.85 and LongMemEval-S temporal-reasoning session recall_any@5 ≥ 0.95.

V7-10.01.section_title: Fusion, reranking, and scoring — no ties, no leaks, every number explainable
V7-10.01.text: Default fusion is weighted Reciprocal Rank Fusion: `rrf(d) = Σ_lanes w_lane / (k + rank_lane(d))`, k = 60, with lane weights from `retrieval_policy/v7` per intent class (all 1.0 unless tuned on the dev split). Raw lane scores are never summed across lanes.

V7-10.02.section_title: Fusion, reranking, and scoring — no ties, no leaks, every number explainable
V7-10.02.text: Degenerate-range normalization (D7-06) is removed. Any per-signal normalization MUST be rank-based or use scope-level calibrated transforms fitted offline; a unit test proves that N candidates with distinct raw signals never collapse to fewer than N distinct final scores unless their full signal vectors are identical.

V7-10.03.section_title: Fusion, reranking, and scoring — no ties, no leaks, every number explainable
V7-10.03.text: A constant signal (present with the same value on ≥ 90% of candidates) contributes zero to ranking; the check is automatic per query and reported in `explain`.

V7-10.04.section_title: Fusion, reranking, and scoring — no ties, no leaks, every number explainable
V7-10.04.text: The fused list is cut to the rerank pool R (budget low = 40, mid = 100, high = 300) before S4.

V7-10.05.section_title: Fusion, reranking, and scoring — no ties, no leaks, every number explainable
V7-10.05.text: No lane may truncate below its budget cap before fusion (D7-11); the fused pool retains lane-rank provenance for every candidate.

V7-10.06.section_title: Fusion, reranking, and scoring — no ties, no leaks, every number explainable
V7-10.06.text: **Feature reranker (S4, always on):** a versioned, deterministic linear or monotone model (`rerank_features/v1`) over: IDF-weighted query-term coverage of the unit; coverage of the unit ∪ its ±1 neighbors; exact phrase / proximity; canonical entity match (IDF-weighted); speaker match for speaker-scoped questions; identifier exact match; temporal proximity to the query window; event-predicate match; supersession state vs intent; corroboration (distinct evidence families); lane agreement count. Weights are fitted on the dev split only (V7-22.09) with a published coefficient table; the model is a policy artifact validated under the V6-03.15 registration flow before it becomes default.

V7-10.07.section_title: Fusion, reranking, and scoring — no ties, no leaks, every number explainable
V7-10.07.text: The feature reranker MUST run in ≤ 3 ms p95 over R = 100 on the reference machine without numpy.

V7-10.08.section_title: Fusion, reranking, and scoring — no ties, no leaks, every number explainable
V7-10.08.text: **Cross-encoder tier (S5, optional):** a local ONNX int8 cross-encoder (≤ 35M parameters; candidates `cross-encoder/ms-marco-MiniLM-L-6-v2`, `ms-marco-MiniLM-L-4-v2`, `jina-reranker-v1-tiny-en`, `mxbai-rerank-xsmall-v1` — license-checked per V7-07.11), pool size selected by the V7-10.14 operating curve (provisional r0 values: ≤ 16 on mid, ≤ 32 on high), length-bucketed batching, hard deadline slice ≤ 90 ms; logits sigmoid-normalized; the S4 score is blended (never discarded) so a CE failure or timeout degrades to S4 order with `coverage.rerank = deadline|unavailable`.

V7-10.09.section_title: Fusion, reranking, and scoring — no ties, no leaks, every number explainable
V7-10.09.text: The CE tier ships enabled in `local_memory_max` only after a paired Track R run shows ≥ +0.03 any@10 and ≥ +0.02 NDCG@10 over S4-only at the pool chosen by V7-10.14; otherwise it remains opt-in with its measured delta published.

V7-10.10.section_title: Fusion, reranking, and scoring — no ties, no leaks, every number explainable
V7-10.10.text: **Bounded multiplicative boosts (S6):** `final = base × (1 + α_r(recency−0.5)) × (1 + α_t(proximity−0.5)) × (1 + α_p(proof−0.5))` with α_r ≤ 0.2, α_t ≤ 0.2, α_p ≤ 0.1 (Hindsight's bounded design, adopted); recency uses the occurred axis when known, else recorded; all three default to neutral (0.5) when their signal is absent. The combined swing MUST stay within [−25%, +30%].

V7-10.11.section_title: Fusion, reranking, and scoring — no ties, no leaks, every number explainable
V7-10.11.text: A pass-through base (no CE) MUST be seeded from fused rank (not a constant) so boosts can never turn ranking into a recency sort (Hindsight's documented trap).

V7-10.12.section_title: Fusion, reranking, and scoring — no ties, no leaks, every number explainable
V7-10.12.text: `Hit.score` MUST be the final score; `Hit.score_detail` carries lane ranks, rrf, features, CE score, boosts. Scores are comparable within a result only; `score_family = ranking/v7` declares this.

V7-10.13.section_title: Fusion, reranking, and scoring — no ties, no leaks, every number explainable
V7-10.13.text: A learned reranker (logistic or gradient-boosted over the same features, trained offline on the dev split and on feedback exposure data) MAY replace `rerank_features/v1` only through the V6 policy-artifact graduation path with a paired Track R and Track Q gate; `learned_active` stays fail-closed otherwise (V6-03.16 carried).

V7-10.14.section_title: Fusion, reranking, and scoring — no ties, no leaks, every number explainable
V7-10.14.text: **Cross-encoder operating curve.** Before any CE pool is a default, the formula search MUST measure k ∈ {0, 16, 32, 64, 128, 300} on the Track R dev split (owned twins, plus public dev splits where O1/O2 allow), reporting any@10, NDCG@10, and CE-stage p95 latency on the reference machine for each k, and the k at which marginal any@10 gain falls below 0.005. The profile default is the smallest k within 0.005 any@10 of the best k on the curve that fits the profile's B-envelope budget; k = 0 is the default when the feature reranker (V7-10.06) ties the curve. k = 300 (Hindsight's default) is part of the ablation, never declined unmeasured. A feature-only reranker and, if a cited paper shows stable transfer, a cross-encoder distilled into the linear feature model are additional arms.

V7-10.15.section_title: Fusion, reranking, and scoring — no ties, no leaks, every number explainable
V7-10.15.text: **Temporal ranking policy arms.** The formula search MUST compare at least: (a) window filter + bucket spread + bounded boosts (`boosts/v1`, Hindsight-style α ≤ 0.2); (b) additive decay with a wide range (Mem0-style, ≈ 1.5× boost to ≈ 0.3× dampening); (c) state-key current/historical labels without decay; (d) no temporal reranking. Each arm reports temporal and knowledge-update recall **and** the false-"current" rate (a superseded value delivered first for a `current_value` question). The constraint that time must not override a strong semantic match is tested explicitly (a fixture where the semantically strongest hit is older than a weak recent hit), not adopted by assertion.

V7-11.01.section_title: Support verdict and abstention — refuse only on structure, never on a brittle floor
V7-11.01.text: The support verdict MUST no longer delete ranked candidates on a literal-coverage floor. It classifies each delivered group as `supported | partial | weak` and the whole result as `ready | insufficient` using only these abstention triggers: (a) a hard-identifier query whose identifier has no exact or normalized match in the eligible corpus; (b) zero eligible candidates after all lanes including fuzzy and dense; (c) a calibrated top-score threshold on the S4/S5 score fitted per encoder tier and profile on the dev split (V7-11.06); (d) an explicit negative-evidence rule (the corpus states the opposite and nothing supports the premise) for `abstain_likely` intents.

V7-11.02.section_title: Support verdict and abstention — refuse only on structure, never on a brittle floor
V7-11.02.text: D7-04 is closed when, on LoCoMo cat 1–4, zero-item `insufficient` results fall from 10.4% to ≤ 1.0% and at least 90% of the 84 BM25-recoverable cases return the evidence in the top 10.

V7-11.03.section_title: Support verdict and abstention — refuse only on structure, never on a brittle floor
V7-11.03.text: `weak` groups are delivered (labeled) when the result has fewer than `limit` supported groups; the caller can request `strict=True` to receive only `supported` (V6 contract carried).

V7-11.04.section_title: Support verdict and abstention — refuse only on structure, never on a brittle floor
V7-11.04.text: Pack-derived hits from governed recall (D7-05) MUST carry their governed support verdict and lane signals into fusion; they are scored like any other candidate.

V7-11.05.section_title: Support verdict and abstention — refuse only on structure, never on a brittle floor
V7-11.05.text: Identifier support (D7-12) MUST accept normalized identifier equivalence (case, separator `-_./ ` variants, leading zeros for numeric ids, URL normalization) with the exact form preferred; each equivalence rule is enumerated and tested.

V7-11.06.section_title: Support verdict and abstention — refuse only on structure, never on a brittle floor
V7-11.06.text: Calibration: each (profile, encoder tier, CE on/off) has a `support_calibration/v2` entry fitted on the dev split with: threshold, expected abstention precision/recall, and validation that it `separates` answerable from unanswerable dev items (V6-03.09 carried); unfitted combinations never abstain on score (trigger c disabled) and report `calibration=unfitted`.

V7-11.07.section_title: Support verdict and abstention — refuse only on structure, never on a brittle floor
V7-11.07.text: Abstention targets (Track R + Track Q): LoCoMo cat 5 correct refusal ≥ 0.90 (SB-11), false abstention on answerable cat 1–4 ≤ 0.03; LongMemEval abstention questions (`_abs`) correct refusal ≥ 0.90.

V7-11.08.section_title: Support verdict and abstention — refuse only on structure, never on a brittle floor
V7-11.08.text: `insufficient` results MUST still return a `missing` descriptor: which query facets (terms, entities, time window, identifier) found no support — enabling the reader or the agent to ask a follow-up instead of hallucinating.

V7-12.01.section_title: Context packs — the fewest tokens that let any reader answer
V7-12.01.text: `search` MUST accept `max_tokens` (default 2,000 on consumer profiles) in addition to `limit`; when both are given, the tighter binds. Token counts use a pinned, dependency-free estimator (`tok/v1`: UTF-8 bytes / 4 with a word-boundary correction) and, when `tokenizers` is installed, a pinned `o200k_base`-compatible count reported alongside.

V7-12.02.section_title: Context packs — the fewest tokens that let any reader answer
V7-12.02.text: Packing is greedy over the final ranking with **skip-long-continue** (an item too large for the remaining budget is skipped and packing continues) and **never-empty** (if nothing fits, the top item is truncated at a sentence boundary with an honest `truncated` flag) — Hindsight's rules adopted.

V7-12.03.section_title: Context packs — the fewest tokens that let any reader answer
V7-12.03.text: Metadata MUST NOT count against `max_tokens`, but the serialized reader view (V7-12.10) reports its total token count separately so callers can budget prompts precisely.

V7-12.04.section_title: Context packs — the fewest tokens that let any reader answer
V7-12.04.text: Duplicate collapse and conflict grouping (V6 F13, I1) carry forward: near-duplicate units collapse to one representative with `collapsed_duplicates`; contrary/superseding evidence is never collapsed away and ships as an atomic group or the result says `conflict_unresolved`.

V7-12.05.section_title: Context packs — the fewest tokens that let any reader answer
V7-12.05.text: **Neighbor windows:** a delivered conversational turn MUST be expandable to its ±N turns (N = 1 default on `mid`, 2 on `high`) within the same session, packed as `context` items that count against the budget but are never ranked independently; D7-21 closes when LoCoMo cat 1 (multi-hop) Track Q improves or holds while tokens stay within SB-15.

V7-12.06.section_title: Context packs — the fewest tokens that let any reader answer
V7-12.06.text: **Session grouping:** items from the same session are grouped under a session header carrying the session date and speakers; groups are ordered by relevance by default and chronologically when the intent is temporal or `history_of`, or when `order="chronological"` is requested.

V7-12.07.section_title: Context packs — the fewest tokens that let any reader answer
V7-12.07.text: Every item MUST carry: stable ref, exact quote bytes (post-authorization), speaker, `recorded_at`, occurred interval + precision, session id/label/date, lifecycle (`current | historical | superseded | disputed`), support label, and a compact pin summary. Missing fields are `null`, never invented.

V7-12.08.section_title: Context packs — the fewest tokens that let any reader answer
V7-12.08.text: Observations, profiles, and standing-query results (V7-14) MAY be delivered ahead of raw units when they are fresh and cover the question, but every such item MUST be followed (budget permitting) by at least one of its pinned supporting units, and MUST carry `derived_view` labeling and its proof count.

V7-12.09.section_title: Context packs — the fewest tokens that let any reader answer
V7-12.09.text: **Computed answers:** for `temporal_point`, `temporal_order`, `duration`, `count_aggregate`, and `current_value` intents, the pack MUST include a `computed` item (timeline table, count with the distinct supporting refs, value with valid-from and the superseded predecessor, or interval arithmetic) whose every input is a delivered, pinned item. A computed item never states anything its inputs do not support.

V7-12.10.section_title: Context packs — the fewest tokens that let any reader answer
V7-12.10.text: A canonical **reader view** serializer (`pack_render/v1`) MUST render the pack into a compact text block for LLM prompts: `# MEMORY (as of <query_time>)` → optional `## COMPUTED` → `## FACTS` (typed/observation lines with dates) → `## EVIDENCE` grouped by session with `[ref] <date> <speaker>: <quote>` → `## CONFLICTS` → `## MISSING`. The block is prompt-cacheable (stable ordering, no volatile ids beyond refs) and its format is versioned; every competitor-comparable Track Q run uses it.

V7-12.11.section_title: Context packs — the fewest tokens that let any reader answer
V7-12.11.text: Budget presets MUST exist for comparability: `tokens_800`, `tokens_2000` (default), `tokens_4096` (Hindsight default parity), `tokens_7000` (Mem0 parity). A Track Q row names its preset.

V7-12.12.section_title: Context packs — the fewest tokens that let any reader answer
V7-12.12.text: Progressive disclosure (V4.5 l0/l1/l2 + `expand`) carries forward; `expand(ref, around=N)` returns neighbors, the full source revision, or supporting pins on demand without re-running ranking.

V7-12.13.section_title: Context packs — the fewest tokens that let any reader answer
V7-12.13.text: The pack is deterministic for a fixed manifest: identical inputs produce byte-identical reader views (SB-20).

V7-12.14.section_title: Context packs — the fewest tokens that let any reader answer
V7-12.14.text: The reader view MUST mark context-only items (neighbors) distinctly from ranked evidence, list derived items with their supporting refs, and never include internal scores, lane names, or policy details (those stay in `explain`).

V7-12.15.section_title: Competitor playbooks — the specific way we beat each one
V7-12.15.text: `Memory.stable_context(max_tokens=1500)` MUST return a deterministic, cache-friendly block (profile, standing rules, freshest observations) that changes only when its inputs change, with a content digest so hosts can detect prefix changes.

V7-13.01.section_title: Write path — deterministic by default, grounded when a model helps
V7-13.01.text: T0 MUST run on every accepted source without any model or network and produce: fielded lexical rows (V7-06.02), canonical entities and aliases (V7-08), dual-axis time and event records (V7-09), polarity/hedge/quote/hypothetical labels (V5 carried), typed memory lines where T1 grammar rules fire (V5 `grounding/v1`), session/episode membership and neighbor links (V7-13.04), duplicate links, and a dense vector for the provisioned tier (V7-07).

V7-13.02.section_title: Write path — deterministic by default, grounded when a model helps
V7-13.02.text: Consumer dialogue MUST become retrievable as first-class evidence units without passing through claim review (D7-20). Claims remain the governed path for curated facts; source units are the default retrieval substrate for conversations and documents. Lanes that previously required active claims (structured, temporal) MUST operate on source-unit projections.

V7-13.03.section_title: Write path — deterministic by default, grounded when a model helps
V7-13.03.text: Unit granularity is configurable and recorded: `turn` (default for messages), `sentence-window` (≤ 3 sentences for long turns and documents, with byte pins into the parent), and `session` (a session-level unit whose text is the ordered turns, used by the session-aggregation lane). The LongMemEval paper's finding (session and fact granularity together beat either) is the default: turn and session units are both indexed.

V7-13.04.section_title: Write path — deterministic by default, grounded when a model helps
V7-13.04.text: Session and episode segmentation: explicit `session_id` wins; otherwise sessions break on time gaps > 30 minutes (configurable) or explicit boundaries in imports. Episodes (topic segments within a session) are computed by a deterministic lexical-cohesion segmenter (TextTiling-class) and are retrievable units with byte pins to their member turns.

V7-13.05.section_title: Write path — deterministic by default, grounded when a model helps
V7-13.05.text: T0 latency budget: all T0 stages for a 1 KiB message complete in ≤ 25 ms of worker CPU at p95 on the reference machine, and the unit is lexical-visible ≤ 150 ms p95 after ack under B1 load (SB-17).

V7-13.06.section_title: Write path — deterministic by default, grounded when a model helps
V7-13.06.text: Every T0 output that can be delivered as text (typed lines, event tuples, observation lines) MUST carry byte-verified pins into retained source bytes (`payload[start:end] == value` plus HMAC slice pins, V5-30/V6-02.02 carried). Unpinnable outputs are inspection-only `unsupported_extraction`.

V7-13.07.section_title: Write path — deterministic by default, grounded when a model helps
V7-13.07.text: T0 MUST classify each unit's perspective: `user_stated`, `agent_stated`, `agent_action` (tool call / confirmation: "I've booked your flight"), `third_party`, `document`, `system`. Agent-generated facts are first-class retrievable evidence (the Mem0 2026 lesson) but remain agent-attributed and never impersonate user statements (V6-01.04 carried).

V7-13.08.section_title: Write path — deterministic by default, grounded when a model helps
V7-13.08.text: T0 MUST detect and index user **preferences** deterministically: first-person preference patterns ("I love/like/prefer/hate/can't stand/usually/always/never …", "my favorite …"), with polarity, object span, and time; these feed the profile lane (V7-14.06) and the `preference` intent.

V7-13.09.section_title: Write path — deterministic by default, grounded when a model helps
V7-13.09.text: Bulk import (`Memory.bulk_add`, importers, V7-21.12) MUST run T0 in batched transactions (≥ 500 units per commit) with the same outputs as the per-add path, and sustain ≥ 2,000 turns/s ingest on the reference machine for LoCoMo-sized messages with dense tier S1.

V7-13.10.section_title: Write path — deterministic by default, grounded when a model helps
V7-13.10.text: T1 MAY add, as separate producers with their own `producer_id` and version: a local NER model (GLiNER-class or spaCy, license-checked) contributing entity spans; a local neural coreference resolver contributing pronoun → antecedent links as a supplement to the T0 sieve (V7-13.20), recommended only if the sieve misses the coreference fixture by more than the declared margin; a local query-independent expansion model (doc2query-class) contributing expansion text stored separately and never delivered as evidence. Every T1 span output is pinned; expansions may rank but never support (V5 `_EVIDENCE_SIGNALS` rule carried).

V7-13.11.section_title: Write path — deterministic by default, grounded when a model helps
V7-13.11.text: T1 runs only in declared profiles, as background jobs on the ordinary lane, with a per-unit CPU budget and a queue-depth cap; T1 lag is reported per scope, and search never waits on T1.

V7-13.12.section_title: Write path — deterministic by default, grounded when a model helps
V7-13.12.text: T2 MAY run an LLM (local via llama.cpp/Ollama-compatible endpoint, or an authorized API) as an asynchronous `extract` job per session window producing **grounded facts**: each fact is a short statement plus one or more **required quote spans** copied verbatim from the source; Verbatim verifies each quote by exact byte match (after `norm/v2` matching projection) and stores the fact only if every quote verifies. Facts with any unverifiable quote are rejected and counted.

V7-13.13.section_title: Write path — deterministic by default, grounded when a model helps
V7-13.13.text: T2 facts carry: subject canon, predicate, object, occurred interval (resolved by `temporal/v2` from the quote, never trusted from the model alone), perspective, confidence, `state_key` for evolving facts (V7-16.03), and extraction provenance (model id, prompt digest, decoding settings). They are `derived_view` items: ranked like units, delivered with their quotes, and retired automatically when any pinned source is held, superseded, or erased.

V7-13.14.section_title: Write path — deterministic by default, grounded when a model helps
V7-13.14.text: T2 is ADD-only (the Mem0 2026 lesson): it never updates or deletes prior facts; lifecycle changes flow only through V7-16 supersession rules and explicit `replaces=`.

V7-13.15.section_title: Write path — deterministic by default, grounded when a model helps
V7-13.15.text: T2 cost and latency are bounded and reported: max calls per session window, max input/output tokens, per-scope daily token budget, deadline, retry cap; the report states $ per 1K adds (SB-18 reports default-profile cost separately as $0).

V7-13.16.section_title: Write path — deterministic by default, grounded when a model helps
V7-13.16.text: T2 outputs are measured: fact precision (quote-verified rate), hallucination rejection rate, and the paired Track Q delta vs T0-only on the dev split. T2 is `recommended` for a profile only if Track Q improves ≥ +2.0 points on LongMemEval-S dev with tokens within SB-15.

V7-13.17.section_title: Write path — deterministic by default, grounded when a model helps
V7-13.17.text: T2 prompts MUST be generic: no benchmark names, no question-type hints, no dataset-specific examples (V7-22.18). The prompt text is versioned and published.

V7-13.18.section_title: Write path — deterministic by default, grounded when a model helps
V7-13.18.text: A model failure or absence yields `extraction=unavailable` on the unit; it never blocks visibility, never fabricates, and never retries unboundedly.

V7-13.19.section_title: Write path — deterministic by default, grounded when a model helps
V7-13.19.text: **Fact-index ablation.** On the owned twins (and permitted public dev splits), Track R MUST be reported for three retrieval units: (a) raw turn / sentence-window units; (b) T0 typed lines plus event records; (c) quote-verified extracted lines when a producer exists (T2, or hand-labeled lines). Hand-labeled lines are an **oracle ceiling**, disclosed as such, never reported as the system, and never fed back into lexicons, prompts, or policy. The quality profile's default unit is the cheapest of (a)–(c) that is within 0.01 any@10 of the best; if (c) wins by more than that, V7-00.11 applies and the result is published.

V7-13.20.section_title: Write path — deterministic by default, grounded when a model helps
V7-13.20.text: **Deterministic coreference sieve (`coref_sieve/v1`, T0).** Third-person pronouns and definite descriptions (`she`, `he`, `they`, `him`, `her`, `his`, `their`, `the new PM`-class nominals) MUST be resolved by a conservative sieve: candidates are canons mentioned in the same session within the previous N turns (N declared, default 6) and in the same unit; filters apply number agreement and gender agreement only where morphology or an explicit statement makes it reliable; ranking uses mention recency, grammatical role (subject > object), speaker alternation (`you`/`I` resolve to the addressee/speaker), and co-occurrence with the candidate canon; if more than one candidate survives within a declared margin, the sieve abstains to `subject=unknown`. Resolved links are pinned (pronoun span → antecedent span). The owned fixture has ≥ 400 pronoun cases written from owned text (never from benchmark gold), including ≥ 100 whose antecedent is beyond the immediately previous turn and ≥ 50 two-candidate traps; precision ≥ 0.95 is required, recall is published. Event records (V7-09.08) and state keys (V7-16.03) use the sieve's resolutions.

V7-14.01.section_title: Consolidation — observations, profiles, standing queries, all grounded
V7-14.01.text: **Observations** are consolidated beliefs over ≥ 2 supporting units from distinct evidence families (V6-03.11/12 carried) about one subject slot (subject canon + predicate family). Each observation stores: text (template-generated on T0; model-generated on T2 only with every clause pinned), the supporting unit refs with quotes, a proof count, first/last supporting occurred times, contradiction refs, and a `stale` flag.

V7-14.02.section_title: Consolidation — observations, profiles, standing queries, all grounded
V7-14.02.text: Observations MUST be re-derivable: T0 observations are deterministic functions of their pins; T2 observations store the prompt digest and are regenerated only by an explicit job. Re-derivation from the same pins yields byte-identical T0 text (V6-03.13(c) carried).

V7-14.03.section_title: Consolidation — observations, profiles, standing queries, all grounded
V7-14.03.text: Freshness: when a new unit arrives in an observation's slot and consolidation has not yet processed it, the observation is marked `stale`; stale observations are delivered only together with the newer units, labeled, or withheld under `strict=True` (Hindsight's freshness rule, made a hard contract).

V7-14.04.section_title: Consolidation — observations, profiles, standing queries, all grounded
V7-14.04.text: Near-duplicate observations MUST be reconciled by deterministic similarity (canonical slot equality + text similarity ≥ 0.9); merge folds evidence sets and keeps both histories; merge is a link, reversible.

V7-14.05.section_title: Consolidation — observations, profiles, standing queries, all grounded
V7-14.05.text: Consolidation runs on the maintenance lane with a utility budget per scope and window (V5 `consolidate_windowed` carried), never blocks writes, and reports backlog: `unconsolidated_units`, oldest age, and throughput. A backlog > 10,000 units or > 1 hour age is a surfaced health warning (the Hindsight #1573 failure mode is detectable, not silent).

V7-14.06.section_title: Consolidation — observations, profiles, standing queries, all grounded
V7-14.06.text: **Profiles:** a per-subject profile view aggregates current preferences, attributes (home city, job, relationships, pets, hobbies), and their histories from T0/T2 facts and observations, each slot pointing to its pinned support and marked `current | historical | disputed`. `Memory.profile(subject=None)` returns it in ≤ 5 ms from a maintained materialization.

V7-14.07.section_title: Consolidation — observations, profiles, standing queries, all grounded
V7-14.07.text: **Standing queries** (Hindsight "mental models"): a caller registers a question; Verbatim stores its current answer pack and rebuilds it in the background when any unit in the query's scope and filters changes (scoped change detection, not a timer). Reading a standing query is a DB read ≤ 2 ms. The stored pack keeps pins; if any pin becomes ineligible the stored answer is withheld until rebuilt.

V7-14.08.section_title: Consolidation — observations, profiles, standing queries, all grounded
V7-14.08.text: Consolidated artifacts (observations, profiles, standing-query packs) are closure members: erase, quarantine, or supersession of any supporting unit retires or withholds them in the same closure (V6-03.13(b) carried); tests cover each artifact kind.

V7-14.09.section_title: Consolidation — observations, profiles, standing queries, all grounded
V7-14.09.text: The profile and observation lanes (L-obs) participate in fusion like any lane; they never replace raw evidence for a question whose intent is `lookup` or `identifier`.

V7-14.10.section_title: Consolidation — observations, profiles, standing queries, all grounded
V7-14.10.text: Consolidation quality is measured: observation precision on a labeled fixture (≥ 0.97 of observation clauses entailed by their pins, judged by the deterministic pin check plus a human-labeled slice of ≥ 200), and the paired Track Q delta with L-obs on vs off.

V7-14.11.section_title: Competitor playbooks — the specific way we beat each one
V7-14.11.text: `agent_belief` observations MUST be labeled as the agent's beliefs, carry confidence derived only from proof count and contradiction count (never model self-report), and be excluded from `user_stated` intents.

V7-14.12.section_title: Competitor playbooks — the specific way we beat each one
V7-14.12.text: Entity pages are standing queries over `profile(subject)` plus top events; they inherit V7-14.07 rebuild and withholding rules.

V7-15.01.section_title: Reflect and the reference reader — answers with receipts
V7-15.01.text: `Memory.reflect(question, *, reader, budget, max_iterations=4, max_tokens)` MAY run a bounded agentic loop over Verbatim tools: `search` (with facet and time arguments), `expand`, `profile`, `standing_query`, `compute` (interval algebra, counts), and `done(answer, citations)`. It requires an explicitly configured reader (local endpoint or authorized API); without one it returns `reflect=unavailable`.

V7-15.02.section_title: Reflect and the reference reader — answers with receipts
V7-15.02.text: Reflect MUST gather evidence before answering (≥ 1 search), cap iterations and tokens, and validate citations: every cited ref MUST be one delivered to the loop in this call and every quoted span MUST byte-match its source; an answer with an invalid citation is rejected and retried once, then returned as `unsupported` (Hindsight validates IDs; V7 validates bytes).

V7-15.03.section_title: Reflect and the reference reader — answers with receipts
V7-15.03.text: Reflect answers carry a `grounding` report: fraction of answer sentences with ≥ 1 valid citation, unsupported sentences, and the abstention decision. `strict=True` removes unsupported sentences.

V7-15.04.section_title: Reflect and the reference reader — answers with receipts
V7-15.04.text: Reflect is optional and never on the `search` hot path. Its latency and token cost are reported per call and in B-envelopes as a separate row.

V7-15.05.section_title: Reflect and the reference reader — answers with receipts
V7-15.05.text: Freshness in reflect: stale observations (V7-14.03) MUST be verified against their newer units before being cited.

V7-15.06.section_title: Reflect and the reference reader — answers with receipts
V7-15.06.text: Standing queries and profiles are consulted first when fresh (Hindsight's retrieval ladder), but raw evidence remains the citation target.

V7-15.07.section_title: Reflect and the reference reader — answers with receipts
V7-15.07.text: **Reference reader** `verbatim_reader/v1` (for benchmarks and as the documented recommended prompt): inputs = question, `query_time`, reader view (V7-12.10); instructions = answer only from memory; use the stated dates and the computed section for date arithmetic; respect precision; prefer `current` over `historical` unless the question asks for history; if the memory lacks the answer say so plainly; cite refs. Output = JSON `{answer, citations[], abstain: bool}` with a plain-text fallback. No benchmark-specific rules, no examples drawn from any benchmark, no answer-format coercions beyond "be concise" (V7-22.18).

V7-15.08.section_title: Reflect and the reference reader — answers with receipts
V7-15.08.text: The reference reader has two variants, both published: `direct` (single call) and `notes` (Chain-of-Note: one short note per session group, then answer), selected per run manifest; the harness MUST report both on LongMemEval-S dev before choosing the primary for SB rows, and MUST NOT switch variants per question.

V7-15.09.section_title: Reflect and the reference reader — answers with receipts
V7-15.09.text: Reader-independence evidence: SB rows MUST include at least two reader models, one open-weight (gpt-oss-20b or gpt-oss-120b, matching Hindsight's published backbones) and one frontier; a claimed architectural win must hold for both.

V7-15.10.section_title: Competitor playbooks — the specific way we beat each one
V7-15.10.text: Reflect MAY accept caller `directives` (plain-language constraints injected into the reference reader as a separate section); directives never change retrieval eligibility.

V7-16.01.section_title: Knowledge updates, contradictions, and "what is true now"
V7-16.01.text: V5/V6 supersession remains authoritative: explicit `replaces=` CAS, reviewed update candidates, and `auto_safe` only under the published twin bound (V6-03.03 carried).

V7-16.02.section_title: Knowledge updates, contradictions, and "what is true now"
V7-16.02.text: The update-candidate detector MUST run outside the add's write transaction (V7-17.10) on a prescanned snapshot with the V6 prescan/replan pattern, and MUST NOT be skipped for performance; its latency is reported per add.

V7-16.03.section_title: Knowledge updates, contradictions, and "what is true now"
V7-16.03.text: **State keys:** facts about an evolving attribute (`<subject canon>/<attribute family>`, e.g. `caroline/relationship_status`, `user/home_city`, `user/job`) MUST share a deterministic state key; T0 rules cover ≥ 40 attribute families with lexicons, T2 facts carry model-proposed keys validated against the family list. A newer unit in the same state key with an incompatible value marks the prior value `historical` with `valid_to = successor.occurred_start` (Mem0's `event_end`, deterministic here) — as a derived lifecycle *label* for ranking and packing; it does not change source lifecycle without the V5 rules.

V7-16.04.section_title: Knowledge updates, contradictions, and "what is true now"
V7-16.04.text: For `current_value` intents, the pack MUST lead with the latest non-disputed value per state key and include the immediate predecessor labeled `historical`; for `history_of` intents, the full chain in order.

V7-16.05.section_title: Knowledge updates, contradictions, and "what is true now"
V7-16.05.text: Contradictions without a clear temporal order (same state key, overlapping validity, different values) ship as a `disputed` group with both sides; the reader view lists them under `## CONFLICTS`.

V7-16.06.section_title: Knowledge updates, contradictions, and "what is true now"
V7-16.06.text: Knowledge-update target: LongMemEval-S knowledge-update Track R session recall_all@10 ≥ 0.95 (both old and new sessions retrieved) and Track Q ≥ 95 with the frontier reader.

V7-16.07.section_title: Knowledge updates, contradictions, and "what is true now"
V7-16.07.text: Twin suite growth: the false-auto-update bound requires ≥ 300 zero-failure twins for < 0.01 upper 95% (V6 twins carried); V7 MUST grow the twin corpus to ≥ 320 cases (hedged, quoted, hypothetical, cross-entity, sarcasm, reported speech) and publish the bound.

V7-17.01.section_title: Performance engineering — the latency and cost envelopes
V7-17.01.text: Every envelope MUST be executed by `eval/v7/envelopes.py` on a quiet tree with the stage profiler on and publish p50/p95/p99, stage breakdown (§04.2 stages), SQL statement count per query, bytes read per query, RSS, and the manifest digest. Misses publish (V6-02.14 rule carried).

V7-17.02.section_title: Performance engineering — the latency and cost envelopes
V7-17.02.text: The V6 envelopes A0/A1/A3 remain executed and reported beside B0–B5 for continuity; their targets are superseded by B0/B2/B3 respectively, with the V6 numbers kept in history.

V7-17.03.section_title: Performance engineering — the latency and cost envelopes
V7-17.03.text: Per-query SQL budget: settled `search` on B1 MUST issue ≤ 40 SQL statements and ≤ 4 transactions/snapshots (D7-23), measured by a statement-counting connection wrapper in tests.

V7-17.04.section_title: Performance engineering — the latency and cost envelopes
V7-17.04.text: All hot-path SQL MUST use prepared, cached statements with covering indexes proven by `EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN` tests (no `SCAN` over units, postings, or vectors on the hot path at B1 scale except the declared dense scan).

V7-17.05.section_title: Performance engineering — the latency and cost envelopes
V7-17.05.text: The consumer path MUST materialize payload quotes once per delivered item per call (D7-22): the verified-bytes cache is keyed by `(source_id, revision, generation)` within the snapshot and shared by typed, source, and pack stages.

V7-17.06.section_title: Performance engineering — the latency and cost envelopes
