V7-17.06.text: Post-delivery work (exposure journal, causal token) stays bounded (`_POST_DELIVERY_WRITE_MS` carried) and MUST be batched into one write per call.

V7-17.07.section_title: Performance engineering — the latency and cost envelopes
V7-17.07.text: Python-level hot loops MUST avoid per-candidate object churn: signals as tuples or arrays; no `typing.Mapping` isinstance in loops (V6 lesson); JSON parses of immutable per-unit fields are content-keyed memos with bounded size.

V7-17.08.section_title: Performance engineering — the latency and cost envelopes
V7-17.08.text: Add-ack p95 targets per envelope above; the ack transaction contains only: authorization, idempotency, durable source bytes, receipt, job enqueue, and session receipt. Everything else is post-ack work.

V7-17.09.section_title: Performance engineering — the latency and cost envelopes
V7-17.09.text: Lexical visibility (FTS rows + statistics) MUST be the first post-ack job for a unit and SHOULD be coalesced: the worker batches pending projections into one transaction per ≤ 5 ms or ≤ 64 units, whichever first, so B2 visibility stays ≤ 150 ms p95 without starving client writes (V6 write-starvation mitigations carried).

V7-17.10.section_title: Performance engineering — the latency and cost envelopes
V7-17.10.text: Update-candidate detection, duplicate linking, and graph-edge maintenance MUST move out of the add transaction into post-ack jobs using the prescan/replan pattern (D7-13). Add-ack latency MUST be flat (α ≤ 0.2) from 1K to 100K units.

V7-17.11.section_title: Performance engineering — the latency and cost envelopes
V7-17.11.text: The managed worker MUST expose backpressure: when queue age exceeds a declared bound, `add` still acks, `AddResult.readiness` reports the lag, and `search` barrier waits remain bounded (V6-02.09 carried).

V7-17.12.section_title: Performance engineering — the latency and cost envelopes
V7-17.12.text: Read snapshots MUST be reused across S2–S8 within one call (one `BEGIN` for the read path, D7-23), with the V6 fork-safety and cross-store wake machinery unchanged.

V7-17.13.section_title: Performance engineering — the latency and cost envelopes
V7-17.13.text: The three V6 post-rank passes (duplicate collapse, conflict labeling, exposure) MUST share one snapshot and one batched query per pass; conflict labeling is skipped with a recorded reason when the scope has zero open update candidates (checked from a maintained counter).

V7-17.14.section_title: Performance engineering — the latency and cost envelopes
V7-17.14.text: The consumer result cache (V6-02.13) SHOULD be enabled by default on `local_memory_quality` after B1-cache passes; it additionally caches `insufficient` results for ≤ 30 s when the scope generation is unchanged (negative caching, D7-15), and never caches `pending`, `partial`, `blocked`, `degraded`, or `unavailable`.

V7-17.15.section_title: Performance engineering — the latency and cost envelopes
V7-17.15.text: A query-analysis memo (normalized query → analysis, temporal resolution excluding `now`) and a lane-result memo keyed by `(scope, generation, stats_version, lane, normalized query, budget)` MUST exist, bounded by bytes, invalidated by generation — never by wall clock alone.

V7-17.16.section_title: Performance engineering — the latency and cost envelopes
V7-17.16.text: Cache failures are performance failures only: every cache hit revalidates eligibility of delivered refs on the caller's snapshot (V6 carried).

V7-17.17.section_title: Performance engineering — the latency and cost envelopes
V7-17.17.text: RSS budgets per envelope above; the stage profiler records peak RSS per stage; no stage may hold O(corpus) Python objects on the hot path.

V7-17.18.section_title: Performance engineering — the latency and cost envelopes
V7-17.18.text: On-disk size: index + derived bytes ≤ 2.5× raw text bytes at B3 with S1 int8 vectors; the breakdown (FTS, trigram, stems, vectors, graph, events, observations) is published.

V7-18.01.section_title: Scale — 1M to 100M tokens without falling off the BEAM cliff
V7-18.01.text: Scale tiers are declared and measured: **T-1M** (≈ 20K units, ≈ 1M tokens), **T-10M** (≈ 200K units), **T-100M** (≈ 2M units or a documented shard-equivalent). Each tier publishes search p50/p95/p99, add-ack p95, lexical-visible p95, peak RSS, bytes per unit, and Track R quality on a scale-graded synthetic suite (V7-18.07).

V7-18.02.section_title: Scale — 1M to 100M tokens without falling off the BEAM cliff
V7-18.02.text: Hierarchical retrieval MUST exist from T-10M: session-level and episode-level units (V7-13.03/04) are retrieved first when the fused top-R at unit level is below a coverage threshold, then descended to member turns; each level is independently eligibility-checked, and a parent score never substitutes for child eligibility (V5 hierarchy rule carried).

V7-18.03.section_title: Scale — 1M to 100M tokens without falling off the BEAM cliff
V7-18.03.text: Time partitioning: FTS, vector, and event indexes MUST support partitioning by `(scope, occurred_year)` or equivalent so temporal-window queries touch only overlapping partitions; partition pruning is visible in `explain`.

V7-18.04.section_title: Scale — 1M to 100M tokens without falling off the BEAM cliff
V7-18.04.text: Sharding protocol above a declared per-file threshold (default 2M units or 20 GiB): multiple SQLite files behind one facade with a shard manifest; cross-shard fusion uses ranks (RRF) and never fabricates global BM25 statistics — per-shard statistics are labeled `shard_local` and the cross-shard merge is documented as approximate for BM25 magnitudes but exact for eligibility (V6-02.04 honesty carried).

V7-18.05.section_title: Scale — 1M to 100M tokens without falling off the BEAM cliff
V7-18.05.text: Compaction: consolidation, statistics maintenance, and graph kNN rebuilds MUST be windowed and utility-budgeted; no job scans a whole scope above T-1M; deferred regions resurface in the backlog report.

V7-18.06.section_title: Scale — 1M to 100M tokens without falling off the BEAM cliff
V7-18.06.text: Forgetting is ranking, never deletion: an optional decay policy (Mem0 decay-style) MAY down-weight idle units within the V7-10.10 bounds; deletion remains closure-only (V6-03.05 carried). Decay curves, exemptions (pinned, checker-attested, disputed), and the per-query effect are reported.

V7-18.07.section_title: Scale — 1M to 100M tokens without falling off the BEAM cliff
V7-18.07.text: A scale-graded synthetic generator (`eval/v7/scalegen.py`) MUST produce coherent multi-session histories at 1M/10M/100M tokens with per-ability probes (extraction, multi-hop, update, temporal, abstention, aggregation, preference, ordering, contradiction, instruction-following), seeded and license-free, so scale evidence never depends on a restricted dataset.

V7-18.08.section_title: Scale — 1M to 100M tokens without falling off the BEAM cliff
V7-18.08.text: BEAM (arXiv 2510.27246; 128K/500K/1M/10M buckets, ten abilities, 2,000 validated questions) is the external scale benchmark once its license is reviewed (V7-22.03); SB-12/SB-13 require it.

V7-19.01.section_title: Trust — the moat nobody else ships in open source
V7-19.01.text: Write-channel screening (V3 `rules_v1` + quarantine, measured 8/8 in V3) MUST be on by default in every profile and extended to a `rules_v2` set covering: instruction injection ("ignore previous…", role hijack, tool-call coercion), exfiltration lures (markdown-image/URL beacons, "send … to"), delayed triggers ("when the user next asks about X, …"), credential/secret formats (≥ 60 patterns, superset of Hindsight's 45), base64/hex/rot-encoded payloads (decode-and-rescan, bounded), homoglyph and zero-width obfuscation, and oversized/size-anomaly payloads.

V7-19.02.section_title: Trust — the moat nobody else ships in open source
V7-19.02.text: Screening outcomes are `allow | label | redact | quarantine | block`, per rule and per namespace policy; unlike Hindsight's partial-batch behavior, a blocked item in a batch MUST be reported per item in `AddResult` (never silently dropped).

V7-19.03.section_title: Trust — the moat nobody else ships in open source
V7-19.03.text: Retrieval-time re-screening MUST apply the current rule set to delivered items so sleeper payloads admitted under an older rule version are withheld on delivery once rules update; a rules upgrade MUST also enqueue a retroactive rescan job over existing units (Hindsight Memory Defense is explicitly not retroactive).

V7-19.04.section_title: Trust — the moat nobody else ships in open source
V7-19.04.text: Assembly-level screening: the pack stage MUST check the reader view for compositional injections spanning items (fragments that are benign alone and instructive together) using a sliding-window rule pass; hits demote or withhold the offending items with `coverage.security`.

V7-19.05.section_title: Trust — the moat nobody else ships in open source
V7-19.05.text: Every delivered item carries a `trust` label (`user_stated`, `agent_stated`, `tool_output`, `document`, `third_party`, `imported_unverified`) and the reader view wraps memory in an untrusted-evidence envelope (V3 `provider.py` precedent) instructing the reader that memory content is evidence, not instructions.

V7-19.06.section_title: Trust — the moat nobody else ships in open source
V7-19.06.text: Poisoning corpus: ≥ 300 attack cases (MINJA-style query-seeded writes, AgentPoison-style trigger passages, PoisonedRAG-style targeted misinformation, delayed triggers, encoded payloads, compositional fragments) and ≥ 600 benign twins; targets: block/withhold ≥ 0.95, benign pass ≥ 0.98, poisoned-answer rate in Track Q with the reference reader ≤ 0.02; rule-of-three bounds published (SB-19).

V7-19.07.section_title: Trust — the moat nobody else ships in open source
V7-19.07.text: Screening latency is part of add-ack (≤ 3 ms p95 for 4 KiB) and of S8 (≤ 1 ms p95); the retroactive rescan is a maintenance job with throughput reported.

V7-19.08.section_title: Trust — the moat nobody else ships in open source
V7-19.08.text: Zero delivered facts without verified pins (SB-19): a test sweeps every Track R/Q run's delivered items and fails on any item whose pins do not re-verify against current source bytes.

V7-19.09.section_title: Trust — the moat nobody else ships in open source
V7-19.09.text: Deletion closure MUST cover every V7 artifact class: fielded FTS rows, stem and trigram shadows, `fts5vocab`-visible terms, statistics aggregates, vector matrices and ANN indexes (rebuild or tombstone + compaction with a bounded window), graph edges, event records, aliases, observations, profiles, standing-query packs, T2 facts, caches, exposure rows, and export bundles. `forget` verify reports each class; any missed class fails G7-09.

V7-19.10.section_title: Trust — the moat nobody else ships in open source
V7-19.10.text: PII/secret redaction (`redact` outcome) MUST store the redacted bytes as the canonical payload *and* keep the original only in the encrypted vault under consent-gated hydration (V3 vault carried); redaction applies retroactively to derived artifacts when a rule is added.

V7-19.11.section_title: Trust — the moat nobody else ships in open source
V7-19.11.text: Access control: namespaces, grants, purposes, and perspectives remain the authorization boundary (V3/V4 carried); tag-based visibility (Hindsight `tags` parity, V7-21.09) is a filter layered on top, never a substitute for authorization.

V7-19.12.section_title: Trust — the moat nobody else ships in open source
V7-19.12.text: Audit: every screening decision, redaction, quarantine, forget, and reflect citation is journaled with receipt ids; `Memory.audit(since=…)` returns them without payload bytes.

V7-19.13.section_title: Trust — the moat nobody else ships in open source
V7-19.13.text: Egress: default profiles perform zero network egress (V6); T2, reflect, S2 model fetch, and hosted comparators run only under V7-00.04 authorizations, and a test asserts zero socket creation on default profiles across the full Track R suite.

V7-19.14.section_title: Trust — the moat nobody else ships in open source
V7-19.14.text: Determinism as trust: identical manifest ⇒ identical packs and identical Track R metrics across three cold runs (SB-20); nondeterministic components (S2/S3 floats, T2, reflect) are excluded from the determinism claim and labeled.

V7-19.15.section_title: Trust — the moat nobody else ships in open source
V7-19.15.text: Attack success is judged on the delivered pack (deterministic rule checks) and, when a reader is authorized, on the reader's output; both rates are published with rule-of-three upper bounds for zero-success classes.

V7-20.01.section_title: Agents, actions, procedures, and many writers
V7-20.01.text: **DolphinBench readiness:** the Hermes provider (`adapters/hermes_v3.py`, `register()` discovery) MUST support the DolphinBench harness end to end: ingest user-message histories message by message, prefetch memory for each task, and expose search/profile/standing-query tools; results report accuracy, memory $, agent $, and median seconds (SB-14).

V7-20.02.section_title: Agents, actions, procedures, and many writers
V7-20.02.text: Action-oriented retrieval: tasks that never mention the remembered fact (DolphinBench's "post the update to the appropriate channel") require **implicit recall**: V7 MUST support `prefetch(task_text, context)` that runs intent-agnostic retrieval over rules, preferences, and procedures (standing instructions such as "put release notes in #eng-releases until deploy is green") and returns a compact `## STANDING RULES` block. Standing rules are detected by T0 imperative/normative patterns ("always", "never", "only until", "channel rule", "don't … unless"), pinned, and scoped by entity/topic.

V7-20.03.section_title: Agents, actions, procedures, and many writers
V7-20.03.text: Procedural memory: V4.5 procedures (reviewed, environment-matched, counterexample-attached, measured negative transfer 6 → 0) carry forward and join fusion as a lane for task-shaped queries; ReasoningBank/AWM-style distillation from completed trajectories with checker-attested outcomes MAY propose procedures, never activate them.

V7-20.04.section_title: Agents, actions, procedures, and many writers
V7-20.04.text: Multi-agent: per-agent views are enforced at eligibility (perspectives), shared scopes use dispute reviews for contradictions, and every cross-principal disclosure lands in the propagation ledger (V3/V4 carried). Agent-private notes need explicit grants (V5 aliases carried).

V7-20.05.section_title: Agents, actions, procedures, and many writers
V7-20.05.text: Coding-agent memory: the Claude Code / Codex / Cursor / Devin CLI integrations (V7-21.10) MUST capture project conventions and decisions as standing rules with file-path scoping, deliverable through `prefetch` at session start and on tool calls.

V7-20.06.section_title: Agents, actions, procedures, and many writers
V7-20.06.text: Implicit-recall fixture: ≥ 200 owned action tests (rule stated once, task years later without cue) with pass-with-history/fail-without verification (DolphinBench's solvability certification, adopted): implicit recall@5 of the governing rule ≥ 0.90.

V7-21.01.section_title: Developer surface and adoption — Mem0-simple, Hindsight-complete, strictly more honest
V7-21.01.text: The front door stays `from verbatim import Memory` → `add` / `search` / `inspect` / `forget` (V6-01.01). V7 adds, without breaking signatures: `search(..., max_tokens=, budget=, as_of=, order=, explain=, hint=)`, `reflect(...)`, `profile(...)`, `standing_query(...)`, `prefetch(...)`, `expand(...)`, `bulk_add(...)`, `audit(...)`.

V7-21.02.section_title: Developer surface and adoption — Mem0-simple, Hindsight-complete, strictly more honest
V7-21.02.text: `add` gains typed conversational arguments (V7-09.02) and accepts a list of messages `[{role|speaker, content, timestamp}]` producing one unit per message in one call.

V7-21.03.section_title: Developer surface and adoption — Mem0-simple, Hindsight-complete, strictly more honest
V7-21.03.text: Quickstart ≤ 8 lines, zero keys, zero services, zero downloads, on Linux x86_64/aarch64, macOS arm64, and Windows x86_64, verified in CI from a clean venv (V6-01.13 extended).

V7-21.04.section_title: Developer surface and adoption — Mem0-simple, Hindsight-complete, strictly more honest
V7-21.04.text: Profiles: `local_memory` (S0 or S1, feature rerank, no models), `local_memory_quality` (S1 static tier required, cache on, all T0 lanes), `local_memory_max` (S2 tier + CE + T1; optional T2/reflect with a configured model). Each profile's lane table, budgets, and envelopes are published; switching profile never changes authorization.

V7-21.05.section_title: Developer surface and adoption — Mem0-simple, Hindsight-complete, strictly more honest
V7-21.05.text: Hindsight-shaped aliases MUST exist for migration: `retain` ≙ `add`, `recall` ≙ `search`, `reflect` ≙ `reflect`, banks ≙ namespaces, `types` filter ≙ unit/derived kind filter, `include_chunks` ≙ `expand`. A `verbatim.compat.hindsight` shim with ≥ 20 conformance tests maps Hindsight client calls onto `Memory`, with unsupported options failing loudly.

V7-21.06.section_title: Developer surface and adoption — Mem0-simple, Hindsight-complete, strictly more honest
V7-21.06.text: `budget="low" | "mid" | "high"` MUST map to lane pool sizes (V7-05.07), rerank pool (V7-10.04), CE usage (off / policy / on), neighbor window, and decomposition depth, documented in one table and exposed in `coverage.budget`.

V7-21.07.section_title: Developer surface and adoption — Mem0-simple, Hindsight-complete, strictly more honest
V7-21.07.text: The Mem0 shim (V6-01.07) MUST be extended to the Mem0 2026 OSS surface actually published (verify at build time against the pinned `mem0ai` 2.1.x API), including `infer`, filters, pagination, `history`, and scoping, with CAS/closure honesty carried.

V7-21.08.section_title: Developer surface and adoption — Mem0-simple, Hindsight-complete, strictly more honest
V7-21.08.text: A Zep/Graphiti-shaped read surface (`graph.search`-like facts/entities/episodes result) MAY be offered by projection over units, events, and entities; it never implies a graph database.

V7-21.09.section_title: Developer surface and adoption — Mem0-simple, Hindsight-complete, strictly more honest
V7-21.09.text: Tags: `add(..., tags=[...])` and `search(..., tags=, tags_match="any|all|exact")` provide visibility filtering (Hindsight parity) layered over authorization (V7-19.11).

V7-21.10.section_title: Developer surface and adoption — Mem0-simple, Hindsight-complete, strictly more honest
V7-21.10.text: Integrations with conformance tests against recorded stubs (never a docs-only matrix): LangChain/LangGraph retriever + memory (exists), LlamaIndex retriever, CrewAI memory, OpenAI Agents SDK tool, Vercel AI SDK (via TS client), Pydantic AI tool, Google ADK (exists), Hermes (exists), MCP server with a consumer profile and an agent profile (`search`, `add`, `profile`, `prefetch`), and coding-agent installers for Claude Code, Codex CLI, Cursor, Cline, and Devin CLI (`verbatim install --host <name>` writes the host's MCP/hook config).

V7-21.11.section_title: Developer surface and adoption — Mem0-simple, Hindsight-complete, strictly more honest
V7-21.11.text: TypeScript SDK: publishable `@verbatim/memory-client` with the full V7 search/add surface over the service, generated types from the Python schema, parity tests, and a documented one-command local service.

V7-21.12.section_title: Developer surface and adoption — Mem0-simple, Hindsight-complete, strictly more honest
V7-21.12.text: Importers: `verbatim import --from mem0|zep|hindsight|letta|jsonl|locomo|longmemeval` with dry-run, per-item provenance-loss disclosure, and speaker/session/time mapping; imported records without original sources are labeled `imported_unverified` and can never be `supported` without a pinned source.

V7-21.13.section_title: Developer surface and adoption — Mem0-simple, Hindsight-complete, strictly more honest
V7-21.13.text: Distribution name: resolved before any public instruction (V6-01.06 carried; PyPI `verbatim` is taken). Extras: `[semantic]` (numpy), `[neural]` (onnxruntime + tokenizers), `[ann]` (usearch or hnswlib or sqlite-vec), `[rerank]`, `[t2]` (local-LLM client), `[service]`, `[dev]`; the base wheel imports none of them.

V7-21.14.section_title: Developer surface and adoption — Mem0-simple, Hindsight-complete, strictly more honest
V7-21.14.text: `verbatim doctor` reports, in ≤ 2 s: profile, tiers provisioned, model hashes, index health, backlog, cache state, last envelope results, and exact remediation commands.

V7-21.15.section_title: Developer surface and adoption — Mem0-simple, Hindsight-complete, strictly more honest
V7-21.15.text: A public benchmark page (`docs/benchmarks.md`) is generated only from executed V7 report artifacts, shows every SB row pass/miss with protocol and manifest digest, and is regenerated per release; hand-edited numbers fail CI.

V7-21.16.section_title: Developer surface and adoption — Mem0-simple, Hindsight-complete, strictly more honest
V7-21.16.text: Docs: concepts, API reference from typed docstrings, "migrate from Mem0", "migrate from Hindsight", "migrate from Zep", "how we benchmark", and "trust model" pages; every code block is executed in CI.

V7-21.17.section_title: Competitor playbooks — the specific way we beat each one
V7-21.17.text: `Memory.events(since=cursor)` MUST expose readiness transitions, screening decisions, supersessions, and forget completions as a pollable cursor stream (webhook parity without a network server); the service surface MAY forward them.

V7-22.01.section_title: Evaluation program — numbers that survive a hostile reproduction
V7-22.01.text: A dataset registry (`eval/v7/datasets.json`) MUST record per dataset: source URL, pinned revision/commit/digest, data license, code license, redistribution permission, local storage policy, and `status ∈ {permitted, permitted_local_only, blocked, unverified}`.

V7-22.02.section_title: Evaluation program — numbers that survive a hostile reproduction
V7-22.02.text: Adapters MUST exist in `eval/v7/` for: LoCoMo (`locomo10.json`), LongMemEval S/M/oracle (`longmemeval_{s,m,oracle}.json`), BEAM, DolphinBench, LongMemEval-V2 (when released data is reviewed), MemoryAgentBench, ConvoMem, and the owned scale generator; each adapter ingests through the public `Memory` API only, preserves speakers/sessions/timestamps via V7-09.02, and exposes gold evidence to the scorer only (never to arms, V5 `public_task` rule carried).

V7-22.03.section_title: Evaluation program — numbers that survive a hostile reproduction
V7-22.03.text: License dispositions as of this snapshot: **LongMemEval** code MIT (github.com/xiaowu0162/LongMemEval) — dataset terms to be confirmed on its Hugging Face card before download; **LoCoMo** CC BY-NC 4.0 (snap-research/locomo LICENSE) — `permitted_local_only` for non-commercial evaluation with attribution *only after owner/legal sign-off*, never redistributed, never committed, derived artifacts redacted; **BEAM** — license unverified, `blocked` until reviewed; **DolphinBench** — license unverified, `blocked` until reviewed; **HaluMem** CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 — `blocked`; **MemoryAgentBench** MIT tag with inherited source terms — `unverified`. The already-downloaded `/tmp/locomo/locomo10.json` MUST be deleted or moved under the permitted-local-only policy once the policy is decided.

V7-22.04.section_title: Evaluation program — numbers that survive a hostile reproduction
V7-22.04.text: The full claimed split rule (V7-03.03) applies to every external suite; partial runs are labeled with covered/uncovered ids.

V7-22.05.section_title: Evaluation program — numbers that survive a hostile reproduction
V7-22.05.text: Owned corpora (license-free, committed) MUST mirror each external benchmark's categories at ≥ 500 questions per suite (`eval/v7/owned_lme_like`, `owned_locomo_like`, `owned_actions`), generated by versioned seeded generators, so every SB row has an owned twin that CI can run without network or restricted data.

V7-22.06.section_title: Evaluation program — numbers that survive a hostile reproduction
V7-22.06.text: DolphinBench MUST be run through the Hermes harness (the same one Mem0 used for its headline row) once licensed and once an agent model is authorized; the Verbatim provider is configured only through documented Hermes settings.

V7-22.07.section_title: Evaluation program — numbers that survive a hostile reproduction
V7-22.07.text: LoCoMo tables MUST print category ids with names per the source-code mapping (1 multi-hop, 2 temporal, 3 open-domain, 4 single-hop, 5 adversarial) and the question count per id (282, 321, 96, 841, 446).

V7-22.08.section_title: Evaluation program — numbers that survive a hostile reproduction
V7-22.08.text: Splits: each external benchmark gets a fixed dev/test partition by conversation or question-group (never by random question) recorded in the registry; all tuning (BM25F weights, lane weights, feature-rerank coefficients, calibration thresholds, reader variant) uses dev only; test is run once per frozen manifest.

V7-22.09.section_title: Evaluation program — numbers that survive a hostile reproduction
V7-22.09.text: Tuning artifacts carry the dev split digest; a test-split run whose artifacts were fitted on data containing test ids fails integrity.

V7-22.10.section_title: Evaluation program — numbers that survive a hostile reproduction
V7-22.10.text: Run manifest (`eval/v7/manifests/<digest>.json`): git rev + dirty flag, dataset digests and split, profile, tiers and model hashes, lane policy digest, reader id + decoding + prompt digest, judge id + prompt digest, seeds, hardware, load, start/end time. Every reported number carries its manifest digest.

V7-22.11.section_title: Evaluation program — numbers that survive a hostile reproduction
V7-22.11.text: Seeds and variance: Track Q rows report the mean over ≥ 3 reader seeds (or temperature 0 with ≥ 3 judge passes) with the spread; judge disagreement rates are published.

V7-22.12.section_title: Evaluation program — numbers that survive a hostile reproduction
V7-22.12.text: Tracks: **R** (retrieval-only, judge-free: evidence any/all@k, recall@k, NDCG@k, MRR at turn and session level; latency; tokens), **Q-open** (open-weight reader, pinned judge), **Q-frontier** (frontier reader, pinned judge), **Q-neutral** (third-party harness run unmodified: Maximem `memory_and_context_eval_harness`, Supermemory `memorybench`, Mem0 `memory-benchmarks` — each with its default prompts), **A** (actions: DolphinBench, owned actions), **B** (envelopes), **T** (trust).

V7-22.13.section_title: Evaluation program — numbers that survive a hostile reproduction
V7-22.13.text: Judges: LongMemEval uses its official per-type judge prompts; LoCoMo uses the widely-used gpt-4o-mini binary CORRECT/WRONG judge at temperature 0 with the prompt text pinned and published; a second judge family is run on a ≥ 200-question slice and the agreement reported; a ≥ 100-question human-adjudicated slice calibrates each judge before the first claim.

V7-22.14.section_title: Evaluation program — numbers that survive a hostile reproduction
V7-22.14.text: Same-reader rule: compared arms in one row MUST use the identical reader, prompt variant, decoding, and token budget preset; a row violating it is `invalid`.

V7-22.15.section_title: Evaluation program — numbers that survive a hostile reproduction
V7-22.15.text: Retrieval-only metrics are mandatory beside every Track Q number (the metric that exposed our V6 loss must never hide behind a reader).

V7-22.16.section_title: Evaluation program — numbers that survive a hostile reproduction
V7-22.16.text: Neutral reader and judge prompts (V7-15.07) are the only prompts used for Track Q rows; any alternative prompt is a separately labeled row.

V7-22.17.section_title: Evaluation program — numbers that survive a hostile reproduction
V7-22.17.text: Statistics: paired comparisons use cluster bootstrap by conversation/persona (≥ 10,000 resamples), McNemar exact tests for binary outcomes, and Bonferroni across the SB family; "beats" requires the lower paired bound > 0 against arms run in-harness (V5 stats carried).

V7-22.18.section_title: Evaluation program — numbers that survive a hostile reproduction
V7-22.18.text: **Anti-gaming tripwire:** CI MUST scan all prompts, rule tables, lexicons, alias tables, and code for benchmark question ids, gold answer strings, benchmark-specific phrasings, and dataset names inside runtime (non-eval) code; any hit fails the build. Runtime code may not branch on dataset identity. Lexicons (V7-09.08, V7-16.03, V7-20.02) are built from owned sources and reviewed for leakage.

V7-22.19.section_title: Evaluation program — numbers that survive a hostile reproduction
V7-22.19.text: Contamination note: every Track Q row states that the reader may have seen the public benchmark in pretraining; owned-twin results are reported beside public results for the same configuration.

V7-22.20.section_title: Evaluation program — numbers that survive a hostile reproduction
V7-22.20.text: Co-reporting: every quality number appears with median/p95 tokens, search p50/p95, write cost, and reader cost for the run (V7-03.04).

V7-22.21.section_title: Evaluation program — numbers that survive a hostile reproduction
V7-22.21.text: Failure analysis: each Track R and Track Q run emits per-question records (permitted fields only for restricted datasets) and an attribution table: `not_indexed`, `not_retrieved`, `retrieved_below_cut`, `packed_out`, `reader_wrong`, `judge_disputed`, `abstained_wrongly` (the V3 F27 attribution method, extended). The attribution drives the next wave (§27).

V7-22.22.section_title: Evaluation program — numbers that survive a hostile reproduction
V7-22.22.text: `eval/v7/track_r.py` MUST run LoCoMo (when permitted) and LongMemEval-S (when permitted) and the owned twins, reporting per category: any@{5,10,20}, all@{5,10,20}, NDCG@10, MRR, zero-result rate, abstention rate, items returned, tokens, and latency; and the same for in-harness baselines: Okapi BM25 (pure Python reference), SQLite FTS5 bm25(), static-dense, BM25+dense RRF, and each V7 ablation.

V7-22.23.section_title: Evaluation program — numbers that survive a hostile reproduction
V7-22.23.text: CI runs the owned-twin Track R suite on every change touching `retrieval/`, `enrichment/`, `storage/`, or `memory/`; a regression > 0.01 any@10 on any category fails the build unless the change carries an approved rationale.

V7-22.24.section_title: Evaluation program — numbers that survive a hostile reproduction
V7-22.24.text: The report generator refuses to render a number that lacks a manifest digest and renders `not_run` for any SB row without an artifact; hand edits are detected by a digest over the rendered tables.

V7-23.01.section_title: Comparator program — run them, pin them, or name them unavailable
V7-23.01.text: Arms to execute in-harness when authorized: `mem0_oss` (mem0ai 2.1.x, infer=True with the pinned local or authorized LLM and embedder; `infer=False` separately disclosed), `hindsight_oss` (`hindsight-all`, Postgres + pgvector local container, pinned LLM and reranker per its docs), `graphiti_oss` (graphiti-core 0.30.x with the embedded Kuzu driver where supported, pinned LLM), `letta_memfs` (pinned), plus always-run offline arms (BM25 reference, FTS5, static-dense, hybrid RRF, `verbatim_v6`, `no_memory`, `full_context` where the reader's context allows).

V7-23.02.section_title: Comparator program — run them, pin them, or name them unavailable
V7-23.02.text: Every comparator row carries the 13 V6 pins plus `reader_prompt_digest` and `budget_preset`; `compare()` refusals (track mismatch, weakened, unpinned, reader mismatch) stay enforced (V6-06.04 carried).

V7-23.03.section_title: Comparator program — run them, pin them, or name them unavailable
V7-23.03.text: Comparator configuration follows each vendor's published best-practice docs at the pinned version; a configuration note is sent to the vendor for review before any public comparison (V4-54.12 carried).

V7-23.04.section_title: Comparator program — run them, pin them, or name them unavailable
V7-23.04.text: Hosted rows (Mem0 Platform, Zep Cloud, Supermemory, Hindsight Cloud) stay `out_of_scope` unless the owner authorizes spend; their published numbers appear only in the §01 register as references, never as rows we "beat".

V7-23.05.section_title: Comparator program — run them, pin them, or name them unavailable
V7-23.05.text: Unavailable arms remain named rows with reasons (V6-06.03 carried).

V7-23.06.section_title: Comparator program — run them, pin them, or name them unavailable
V7-23.06.text: Cost parity: each arm reports extraction/embedding/reader tokens and $ per 1K adds and per 1K queries at pinned pricing dates; unmeasured categories are labeled, never zero.

V7-23.07.section_title: Comparator program — run them, pin them, or name them unavailable
V7-23.07.text: Latency parity: each arm's search and add latency is measured on the reference machine with its local services; hosted-network latency is never compared to local latency.

V7-24.01.section_title: Category attack plans — how each benchmark slice is won
V7-24.01.text: A speaker-attribution check MUST exist in the verdict (V7-11): for questions whose parsed subject is a speaker canon, groups whose evidence is spoken only by a different speaker are labeled `speaker_mismatch`, packed after matching-speaker evidence, and surfaced in `missing` when no matching-speaker evidence exists.

V7-24.02.section_title: Category attack plans — how each benchmark slice is won
V7-24.02.text: Image-bearing turns: the BLIP caption text (and the search query, if present) MUST be indexed as a separate low-weight field of the turn (LoCoMo turns include `blip_caption`), labeled as machine-generated description, never as the speaker's words.

V7-24.03.section_title: Category attack plans — how each benchmark slice is won
V7-24.03.text: LoCoMo temporal answers are session-date-relative; the reader view MUST show every item's session date and the resolved occurred interval, and computed items MUST keep relative anchoring when the source phrase is relative — rendering both the resolved interval and the anchor date it was resolved against — without ever increasing precision (V7-09.12).

V7-24.04.section_title: Category attack plans — how each benchmark slice is won
V7-24.04.text: The LongMemEval adapter MUST pass `question_date` as `query_time`/`as_of`, each session's `haystack_dates` entry as `session_started_at`, and each turn's role as speaker (`user` / `assistant`), and MUST score turn-level recall from `has_answer` and session-level recall from `answer_session_ids`.

V7-24.05.section_title: Category attack plans — how each benchmark slice is won
V7-24.05.text: LongMemEval-M (≈ 500 sessions per question) is the scale probe for B3-class behavior on a public set; it is reported as its own row with the same targets relaxed by at most 3 points, the relaxation stated.

V7-24.06.section_title: Category attack plans — how each benchmark slice is won
V7-24.06.text: The BEAM adapter MUST report per ability and per scale bucket. Mechanism mapping (ability names to be verified against the released data): information extraction → V7-24.1 single-hop stack; multi-session reasoning → session units + facets; knowledge update → state keys; temporal reasoning and event ordering → event records + algebra; contradiction resolution → disputed groups; abstention → V7-11; preference following → profile lane; instruction following → standing rules (V7-20.02); summarization → session/episode units + observations with pins.

V7-24.07.section_title: Category attack plans — how each benchmark slice is won
V7-24.07.text: Scale behavior: the drop from the 1M to the 10M bucket MUST be ≤ 8 points (Mem0's published drop is 15.5) at the same reader; retrieval latency at 10M stays within B5.

V7-24.08.section_title: Category attack plans — how each benchmark slice is won
V7-24.08.text: Mechanism: standing-rule detection and `prefetch` (V7-20.02), preference and profile lanes, entity facts about tools/channels/people, and per-task implicit recall; the Hermes provider injects the `## STANDING RULES` and a ≤ 1,500-token memory block per task.

V7-24.09.section_title: Category attack plans — how each benchmark slice is won
V7-24.09.text: Target SB-14; failure attribution must separate `rule_not_indexed`, `rule_not_prefetched`, `agent_ignored_memory`, and `tool_error`.

V7-24.10.section_title: Category attack plans — how each benchmark slice is won
V7-24.10.text: `owned_actions` (≥ 500 tests) and `owned_preferences` (≥ 300 tests) are CI-runnable twins of DolphinBench and LME preference questions; pass-with-history / fail-without certification is mandatory for every test (DolphinBench solvability rule adopted).

V7-24.11.section_title: Category attack plans — how each benchmark slice is won
V7-24.11.text: **Preference pack shape.** For `preference` intents the pack MUST lead with the matching profile slot(s) (V7-14.06), then applicable standing rules (V7-20.02), then the supporting pinned turns, each labeled; the reference reader applies them (V7-15.07). Personality disposition stays declined (V7-15.10). Single-session-preference (LongMemEval) and `owned_preferences` MUST be reported as their own rows in every Track R and Track Q table and in the formula search, so a lexical win cannot hide a preference loss.

V7-25.01.section_title: Competitor playbooks — the specific way we beat each one
V7-25.01.text: Beat on Q-neutral (SB-08) with the harness they did not tune; beat on tokens (SB-15) at equal or higher accuracy; beat on write cost (SB-18) and latency (SB-16/17); match their shim surface so migration is one import change (V7-21.07).

V7-25.02.section_title: Competitor playbooks — the specific way we beat each one
V7-25.02.text: Run `mem0_oss` in-harness (V7-23.01) on Track R and Track Q with the same reader; publish both our win and any loss by category.

V7-25.03.section_title: Competitor playbooks — the specific way we beat each one
V7-25.03.text: Beat on Track Q with their own published backbones (gpt-oss-20b, gpt-oss-120b; SB-04, SB-05, SB-09) — the only apples-to-apples comparison their paper enables.

V7-25.04.section_title: Competitor playbooks — the specific way we beat each one
V7-25.04.text: Beat on recall latency by ≥ 10× at equal Track R quality (B1 p95 ≤ 40 ms vs their 100–600 ms) and on write latency by ≥ 20× (SB-17).

V7-25.05.section_title: Competitor playbooks — the specific way we beat each one
V7-25.05.text: Match every Hindsight retrieval idea deterministically: four-way retrieval (V7-06/07/08/09), RRF k=60 (V7-10.01), bounded multiplicative boosts (V7-10.10), time-bucket spread (V7-09.06), token-budget packing with skip-long-continue (V7-12.02), budget tiers (V7-21.06), trace (V7-05.15), observations with proof counts and freshness (V7-14), mental models (V7-14.07), reflect with citation validation — upgraded to byte validation (V7-15.02).

V7-25.06.section_title: Competitor playbooks — the specific way we beat each one
V7-25.06.text: Run `hindsight_oss` in-harness (V7-23.01) with its documented local reranker and an authorized LLM; publish head-to-head Track R, Track Q, B-envelope, and resource rows.

V7-25.07.section_title: Competitor playbooks — the specific way we beat each one
V7-25.07.text: Beat on LME-S with the same reader (gpt-4o, SB-06); beat on visibility latency (lexical-visible ≤ 150 ms vs asynchronous episodes); match bi-temporal semantics (V7-09.01, V7-16.03) and the FACTS/ENTITIES context shape (V7-12.10) at ≤ 2K tokens.

V7-25.08.section_title: Competitor playbooks — the specific way we beat each one
V7-25.08.text: Publish a `tokens_800` operating point (SB-15) on LME-S and run MemoryBench unmodified (Q-neutral); compare only in-harness.

V7-25.09.section_title: Competitor playbooks — the specific way we beat each one
V7-25.09.text: Beat on tokens at matched accuracy with the same reader (≤ 2K vs their ~30–40K standing context); offer a prompt-cacheable `stable_context` mode (profile + standing rules + top observations, ≤ 1,500 tokens, deterministic ordering) for agents that prefer a fixed prefix (V7-12.15).

V7-25.10.section_title: Competitor playbooks — the specific way we beat each one
V7-25.10.text: Match the event-calendar structure deterministically (V7-09.08/09) and the loop with bounded reflect (V7-15.01); target SB-07 ≥ 95.0 with ≤ 4 reflect iterations and ≤ 6K tokens per question, reporting per-question latency and cost beside accuracy.

V7-25.11.section_title: Competitor playbooks — the specific way we beat each one
V7-25.11.text: Letta (MemFS): provide a file-native projection (`verbatim export --markdown <dir>` + re-import through the screened write channel) so file-oriented agents get grep-able memory without losing provenance; Cognee/LangMem: shims only if demand appears; AWS AgentCore / Vertex Memory Bank: position on offline operation, provenance, and deletion closure — no hosted comparison without authorization.

V7-26.01.text: Developer preview needs G7-00, G7-01, G7-04, G7-06, G7-09. "Faster than Hindsight/Mem0/Zep" needs G7-04 plus that vendor's in-harness latency row (G7-12 latency part). "More accurate than <vendor>" needs G7-10 or G7-11 plus G7-12 for that vendor. "State of the art on <benchmark>" needs the SB row, the full split, the neutral harness row (Q-neutral) where one exists, and expires in 90 days (V4 TTL carried).

V7-26.02.text: Gates are evaluated by `eval/v7/gates.py`, which reads only executed artifacts and the ledger; a gate with any `not_run` input is `not_run`, never `passed`.

V7-26.03.text: Until owner decision O9 accepts a formula-search report, every published quality number MUST carry `formula=unselected` and the provisional tag set it ran under. No retrieval-only artifact may satisfy G7-10 or G7-11, and no Track R result may be worded as a Mem0-level or Hindsight-level result (V7-26.01).

V7-27.01.section_title: Build program — phases, waves, and how parallel work stays correct
V7-27.01.text: Work is executed in waves of parallel workers (up to 50 concurrent, all SWE-2 Max per owner instruction), each with a disjoint ownership map declared in `docs/v7_contracts.md` before the wave starts. Two workers never own the same file.

V7-27.02.section_title: Build program — phases, waves, and how parallel work stays correct
V7-27.02.text: Wave 0 (audit, ≤ 12 workers, read-only): complete the defect register D7-25+, map every hot-path SQL statement, record current stage timings, and draft owned-twin generators' category specs.

V7-27.03.section_title: Build program — phases, waves, and how parallel work stays correct
V7-27.03.text: Every worker brief MUST include: the requirement ids it closes, its owned files, the frozen interfaces it must not change, the tests it must add (failing first), the exact verification commands, and the quiet-tree rule for measurements. Workers MUST NOT run envelopes or Track R suites while other workers edit (V6-00.07); measurement is a separate, serialized wave.

V7-27.04.section_title: Build program — phases, waves, and how parallel work stays correct
V7-27.04.text: Integration is performed only in the main session: after each wave the main session reviews every diff against its brief, runs the focused suites, then the full suite, then the owned-twin Track R suite, and records before/after numbers in the ledger. A worker's self-reported result is never evidence.

V7-27.05.section_title: Build program — phases, waves, and how parallel work stays correct
V7-27.05.text: Any worker change that moves an owned-twin Track R category by > 0.01 in either direction MUST be explained in its report with the attribution class that moved.

V7-27.06.section_title: Build program — phases, waves, and how parallel work stays correct
V7-27.06.text: Measurement waves run alone: no editing workers, no competing pytest, load recorded; polluted runs are discarded (V6-00.07).

V7-27.07.section_title: Build program — phases, waves, and how parallel work stays correct
V7-27.07.text: The full test suite (≥ 2,700 tests today) plus the mutation suite MUST be green at every wave boundary; a wave does not close on a red suite.

V7-29.01.section_title: Claims ladder — what may be said, when
V7-29.01.text: Every public sentence links to the report row that backs it; a sentence whose row turns `stale` (V7-00.10) or `missed` is withdrawn in the next release.

V7-29.02.section_title: Claims ladder — what may be said, when
V7-29.02.text: Vendor-published numbers may be quoted only with their provenance tag, date, and reader model, and never as a row in our results table.

V7-30.01.text: `units` MUST be derivable from `sources` + `source_revisions` alone (plus the add-time conversational arguments stored with the source); dropping every V7 table and re-running projection reproduces them byte-identically at the same generation.

V7-30.02.text: Every V7 table carries `generation` and participates in the V5 generation fence; a projection rebuild writes a new generation and flips atomically.

V7-30.03.text: Every V7 table has covering indexes for its hot-path access pattern, asserted by `EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN` tests (V7-17.04).

V7-30.04.text: Migration from V6 stores re-projects lazily per scope with a resumable cursor; searches during migration use the V6 path for unmigrated scopes and report `coverage.migration=partial`.

V7-31.01.text: `SearchResult` gains: `reader_view: str` (V7-12.10, rendered lazily on access), `tokens: {items, reader_view}`, `computed: list[ComputedItem]`, `missing: MissingDescriptor | None`, `coverage.{policy, lanes, budget, temporal, entities, facets, rerank, dense, security, migration}`, and `explain` payload when requested. Existing fields keep their meaning.

V7-31.02.text: `Hit` gains: `unit_id`, `speaker`, `perspective`, `session: {id, label, started_at}`, `occurred: {start, end, precision, source}`, `recorded_at`, `lifecycle_label ∈ {current, historical, superseded, disputed}`, `trust`, `context: list[ContextItem]` (neighbors), `derived: bool`, `proof_count`.

V7-31.03.text: `ComputedItem = {kind: timeline|count|current_value|order|duration, text, inputs: [ref], formula}`; every input ref appears in `items` or `context`.

V7-31.04.text: `ReflectResult = {answer, citations: [{ref, quote, byte_range}], abstain, grounding: {cited_sentences, total_sentences, unsupported}, iterations, tokens, latency_ms, reader_id}`.

V7-31.05.text: All new result types serialize through the canonical `json_dumps` seam and are exposed identically over the `/v2/memory/*` service (new routes `/v2/memory/expand`, `/profile`, `/prefetch`, `/stable_context`, `/reflect`, `/audit`, `/events`), MCP, and the TS client; one schema, one serializer (V6-05.02 carried).

V7-31.06.text: Every new argument is validated with typed errors (`VALIDATION`, `CAPABILITY_UNAVAILABLE`, `NOT_FOUND_OR_UNAUTHORIZED`); unknown arguments fail; no argument widens authorization.

V7-31.07.text: `budget`, `preset`, and `max_tokens` are recorded in `coverage` exactly as applied, so any caller can reproduce a result's configuration.

V7-32.01.text: Every tag defined in §32.2–§32.13 (`bm25f/v1`, `retrieval_policy/v7`, `rerank_features/v1`, `boosts/v1`, `graph_ppr/v1`, `alias/v1`, `ident_eq/v1`, `temporal/v2` rule set, `event/v1`, `state_keys/v1`, `pref/v1`, `rules_detect/v1`, `intent/v2`, and the CE pool row of §32.3) carries status `provisional/v7-r0`. Artifacts produced under them record that status.

V7-32.02.text: Shipping tags are bound only by an offline **formula search** run on the dev split (V7-22.08) after the D7 retrieval fixes land (P2 exit). Tuning on test remains forbidden (V7-22.09). The winning definition is pasted into §32 under a new version (`…/v2` or a dated policy id); the `…/v1` snapshot moves to an appendix and stays reproducible. The search manifest digest is recorded beside every winning tag.

V7-32.03.text: The formula search MUST answer, with citations, ablation tables on our store, latency on the reference machine, and complexity, in priority order: **Q1** default fusion (RRF, weighted RRF, CombSUM on calibrated scores, or the linear feature model), its k, and per-intent weights, measured on eligible-corpus BM25; **Q2** the first shippable offline semantic tier (static mean-pool, distilled student, SPLADE-class learned sparse expansion, small-matrix late interaction, or exact cosine over a small ONNX bi-encoder), with any@10 gain on open-domain and paraphrase slices, encode latency, and resident bytes per 100K units; **Q3** the cross-encoder curve (V7-10.14); **Q4** entity resolution (V7-08.13); **Q5** temporal ranking policy (V7-10.15) with the false-current rate; **Q6** graph method — SQL link expansion (Hindsight-style shared-entity / kNN / causal score) vs bounded PPR vs entity-overlap only, with hop limit, fan-out cap, and ms at 10K and 100K units; **Q7** the unit ablation (V7-13.19); **Q8** the coreference sieve vs previous-turn-only on the owned fixture (V7-13.20); **Q9** a written rejection list of algorithms that need a graph database, a vector server, a network call on the default path, approximate authorization, or an unpinned generated sentence as the only trace.

V7-32.04.text: The search report is a decision record: for each question, the arms run, the metric table (every LoCoMo/LongMemEval category reported separately, preference rows included, V7-24.11), the winner, the runner-up margin, the latency cost, and each rejected alternative with the metric that rejected it. A question with no arm beating the r0 snapshot by more than noise keeps the snapshot and says so.

V7-32.05.text: The spec editor MUST NOT invent winning weights while the search is open, and the search MAY read public papers but MUST NOT paste their task-specific rules, gold synonyms, or benchmark-derived lexicon entries into Verbatim (V7-22.18).

V7-32.06.text: Indexes and derived artifacts built under a provisional tag and under a selected tag MUST NOT be mixed in one ranking space: rows from the other tag are `excluded_generation` until re-projected (the V7-07.13 rule, extended to every §32 tag).

V7-33.01.text: **Evidence any@k** — for a question with gold evidence set G (LoCoMo `evidence` dialog ids, LongMemEval `has_answer` turns or `answer_session_ids` sessions), 1 if at least one element of G appears among the first k *distinct* delivered units (after mapping units to their gold granularity), else 0; averaged over questions with non-empty G.

V7-33.02.text: **Evidence all@k** — 1 if every element of G appears in the first k distinct delivered units; averaged likewise. Multi-hop rows MUST report all@k beside any@k.

V7-33.03.text: **Recall@k (LongMemEval)** — `recall_any` and `recall_all` exactly as the official retrieval scripts compute them at turn and session granularity; NDCG@k with binary relevance and the ideal DCG over G.

V7-33.04.text: **MRR@k** — mean reciprocal rank of the first gold unit within k (0 if absent).

V7-33.05.text: **Zero-result rate** — fraction of answerable questions (non-empty G) whose result has zero delivered items; **false abstention** — fraction of answerable questions whose status is `insufficient`; **correct refusal** — fraction of unanswerable questions (LoCoMo cat 5, LongMemEval `_abs`) whose status is `insufficient` or whose reader output abstains.

V7-33.06.text: **Delivered tokens** — `tok/v1` count of the reader view actually passed to the reader (not the pack's raw bytes), median and p95 per question; **items delivered** — distinct units + derived items in the pack.

V7-33.07.text: **Latency** — wall time of `Memory.search` from call entry to return on the reference machine, settled store unless the row states otherwise; reader and judge latency reported separately; end-to-end question latency = search + reader.

V7-33.08.text: **Accuracy (Track Q)** — the benchmark's official judge verdicts (LongMemEval per-type prompts; LoCoMo binary J) averaged over the full split; per-category tables are micro-averaged within category, and the overall is micro over questions unless the benchmark defines otherwise, with the averaging stated.

V7-33.09.text: **Cost** — tokens × pinned price per million for reader, judge, T2 extraction, and embeddings separately, per 1K questions and per 1K adds; local models report CPU-seconds instead of dollars.

V7-33.10.text: **Grounding rate** — fraction of delivered textual items whose pins re-verify (must be 1.0); **citation validity** (reflect) — fraction of cited refs delivered in the call with byte-matching quotes.

V7-33.11.text: **Stage α** — the log-log slope of a stage's mean time versus corpus size over ≥ 4 checkpoints; α > 1.0 is superlinear (V6-02.16 method carried).

V7-34.01.section_title: Reference reader and judge prompts (normative drafts; versioned `verbatim_reader/v1`, `verbatim_judge_locomo/v1`)
V7-34.01.text: The judge prompt contains no instruction to lean toward either verdict and no dataset-specific equivalence lists (the Maximem audit finding, V7-01.02). LongMemEval rows use the official per-type judge prompts from the pinned repository commit unmodified.

V7-34.02.section_title: Reference reader and judge prompts (normative drafts; versioned `verbatim_reader/v1`, `verbatim_judge_locomo/v1`)
V7-34.02.text: Reader decoding for Track Q: temperature 0 (or the provider minimum), max output tokens 512 (notes variant 1,024), JSON mode when the provider supports it; malformed JSON falls back to plain-text answer extraction by a published rule, counted in the report.

V7-34.03.section_title: Reference reader and judge prompts (normative drafts; versioned `verbatim_reader/v1`, `verbatim_judge_locomo/v1`)
V7-34.03.text: The reader view is inserted verbatim; no Verbatim code may add hints derived from the question type into the prompt beyond the reader view itself.

V7-34.04.section_title: Reference reader and judge prompts (normative drafts; versioned `verbatim_reader/v1`, `verbatim_judge_locomo/v1`)
V7-34.04.text: Verbatim resolves `time_phrase` itself with `temporal/v2`; model-computed dates are never stored (V7-13.13). Quotes are verified by V7-13.12 before any fact is stored.

V7-35.01.text: Every V7 mutation target listed above MUST be added to `eval/v7/mutations.yaml` with an anchor occurring exactly once and a `killed_by` test (V4 mutation discipline carried; the MUT-10 lesson: anchors must follow refactors and the killing test must exercise the anchored path).

V7-35.02.text: Property tests use a fixed seed recorded in the manifest; failing seeds are added as regression fixtures.

V7-36.01.section_title: Wave plan (execution sketch; adjusted per wave review)
V7-36.01.text: Each wave's briefs are written by the main session from this table, list requirement ids and owned files, and are archived under `eval/v7/waves/<wave>.md` with the review outcome of every worker.

V7-36.02.section_title: Wave plan (execution sketch; adjusted per wave review)
V7-36.02.text: A wave closes only when: every worker's diff is reviewed, focused suites pass, the full suite and mutation suite pass, owned-twin Track R shows no category regression > 0.01 (or an approved rationale), and the ledger rows it touched are updated with evidence.

H01.text: Typed lane returns a full pool; lexical and dense lanes still run and appear `ok` in coverage (D7-09)

H02.text: A slow lane exhausts only its own deadline slice; other lanes return full results (D7-14)

H03.text: Leave-one-lane-out table generated on owned twins with per-category deltas

H04.text: Possessive query "What is Caroline's job?" reaches `caroline` postings; no `s` term appears (D7-01, D7-03)

H05.text: Lowercase "what did caroline paint" yields entity signal equal to the capitalized query (D7-02)

H06.text: Stemmed match: "decided" query retrieves a "decide" turn with a lower score than an exact "decided" turn

H07.text: Typo "persue" respelled to "pursue"; evidence retrieved in top 10; fuzzy lane disclosed

H08.text: Speaker field: "What did Melanie say about pottery" ranks Melanie's pottery turn above Caroline's pottery turn

H09.text: BM25F weights loaded from `bm25f/v1`; changing a weight changes ranking deterministically

H10.text: Incremental statistics: after 1,000 adds, df/avgdl equal a full recomputation exactly

H100.text: Artifacts under `provisional/v7-r0` and under a selected tag cannot share a ranking space; the other tag's rows are `excluded_generation`

H101.text: Entity resolution: same-name-different-person fixture over-merge rate ≤ 0.01; ambiguous pairs stay separate or become candidates

H102.text: A model-proposed causal link is stored as a pinned `causal_candidate`, never used for eligibility, and absent from the graph lane until its ablation passes

H103.text: Preference question pack leads with the profile slot, then the standing rule, then pinned supporting turns; preference rows reported separately

H104.text: Before O9, every published quality number carries `formula=unselected`; G7-02 cannot pass without the formula-search artifact

H11.text: Held source excluded from statistics or `stats=exact_recomputed` reported; never universe stats silently

H12.text: Frequent-speaker dominance fixture: evidence turn outranks ≥ 90% of speaker-only turns (D7-07)

H13.text: Distinct raw signals never collapse to tied final scores (D7-06)

H14.text: Constant signal detected and zero-weighted in `explain`

H15.text: Lane pools respect budget low/mid/high caps and report them

H16.text: RRF fusion reproduces a hand-computed ranking on a fixed fixture

H17.text: Feature reranker coefficients load from a registered policy artifact; unregistered artifact refused

H18.text: CE timeout degrades to S4 order with `coverage.rerank=deadline`; no eligibility change

H19.text: Boost bounds: combined swing stays within [−25%, +30%] on adversarial signal inputs

H20.text: Pass-through base never becomes a pure recency sort

H21.text: Zero-result rate on LoCoMo-like owned twin ≤ 1% (D7-04)

H23.text: Normalized identifier equivalence (`ABC-123` vs `abc_123`) supports delivery (D7-12)

H24.text: Calibrated threshold unfitted ⇒ no score-based abstention and `calibration=unfitted`

H25.text: Governed-lane pack hits carry signals into fusion (D7-05)

H26.text: `weak` groups delivered labeled when fewer than `limit` supported groups exist; `strict=True` removes them

H28.text: Relative "yesterday" in a turn from a session dated 2023-05-08 resolves to 2023-05-07 with rule id

H29.text: "last spring" at query time 2024-02-10 resolves to 2023-03-01..2023-05-31 (northern)

H30.text: Month-only mention never renders as a specific day in a computed answer

H32.text: Interval algebra property tests green (containment, order, duration, month arithmetic)

H33.text: Event record extracted for "I joined the pottery class last week" with pinned subject/predicate/object/interval

H34.text: "Which came first" returns both events and the computed order

H35.text: Temporal-window query spreads results across ≥ 4 buckets

H36.text: `current_value` leads with the latest state-key value and includes the labeled predecessor

H37.text: Disputed state (overlapping validity, different values) ships as a `disputed` group

H38.text: Alias rule merges `Mel` → `Melanie` from an explicit "call me Mel" statement; ambiguous alias becomes a candidate

H39.text: Graph PPR retrieves a second-hop turn that shares no query terms but shares an entity chain

H40.text: Purged unit breaks every graph path through it; neighbors not surfaced via it

H41.text: Causal edge created only from an explicit connective with both clauses pinned

H42.text: Contiguous matrix scoring equals the per-row oracle ordering on a fixed corpus

H43.text: int8 scan + rescore recall@50 loss ≤ 1.0 pt vs exact

H44.text: ANN enabled only above threshold; eligibility re-checked exactly on every ANN candidate
